Peter, Elon Musk sparked a __**HUGE**__ conversation on Joe Rogan about immigration policy, government systems, and the real threats to voting...

He highlighted concerns that **open borders allow non-citizens to flood in and affect our democracy, including potentially influencing votes.**

Musk explained: **_“That’s why they want open borders... That’s why some leaders changed their views on borders. That’s the reason—to bring in more people who could affect our systems.”_**

That's why Congress passed the SAVE Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act) in the House — a game-changing bill to require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship before anyone can register to vote.

_But the Senate is stalling_ — _**and we can't let that happen.**_

With millions at stake, we need massive pressure **NOW** to force a vote and _**get the SAVE Act to the President's desk.**_

Backed and authored by **House Freedom Caucus member Rep. Chip Roy** , the SAVE Act fights back against the very threats Elon Musk exposed on Rogan—requiring ironclad citizenship proof to protect your vote.

clean_body: | | | Peter, Elon Musk sparked a HUGE conversation on Joe Rogan about immigration policy, government systems, and the real threats to voting... He highlighted concerns that open borders allow non-citizens to flood in and affect our democracy, including potentially influencing votes. Musk explained: “That’s why they want open borders... That’s why some leaders changed their views on borders. That’s the reason—to bring in more people who could affect our systems.” That's why Congress passed the SAVE Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act) in the House — a game-changing bill to require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship before anyone can register to vote. But the Senate is stalling — and we can't let that happen. With millions at stake, we need massive pressure NOW to force a vote and get the SAVE Act to the President's desk. Backed and authored by House Freedom Caucus member Rep. Chip Roy , the SAVE Act fights back against the very threats Elon Musk exposed on Rogan—requiring ironclad citizenship proof to protect your vote. That's why we're calling for 10,000 Americans to sign our petition in the next 10 minutes — a critical step in demanding the Senate act, amplifying this fight for American voters FIRST. name: Nikki Fried, FDP
subject: Democrats win BIG in Florida
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| Friend,

History was just made in Florida!

During Tuesday’s Special Elections, **Emily Gregory won the race for Florida House District 87,** right in Donald Trump's backyard. Mar-a-Lago will now be represented by a Democrat in the Florida House. Democrats swung this seat to the left by double digits, in a district that was supposed to be out of reach.

**Brian Nathan also pulled off an upset in Tampa's Senate District 14,** a seat formerly held by Florida’s Lt. Governor Jay Collins, proving once again that Democrats can run and win anywhere.

This is what year-round organizing looks like. This win is proof of what we can accomplish when we organize early, often, and everywhere.

Floridians are tired. They're tired of the chaos, the corruption, and the sky-high cost of groceries, gas, and healthcare. This week, they voted for something different.

They voted for Emily Gregory, even in Trump’s backyard, and they voted for a Florida we can all afford. We're not stopping here. All across the country, Democrats’ results have shown that no race is out of reach.

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Judicial Watch’s Historic Day at the Supreme Court
body:
Zero Illegal Aliens Released Into U.S. for Tenth Consecutive Month

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH’S HISTORIC DAY AT THE SUPREME COURT

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37440&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS9BWjJSOXprdFRpUT91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=03b3f74ad3881a3da7ca2dfd1829e025635add7551138cf737bc910f86557385]

Our chief investigative reporter, Micah Morrison, recounts
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37435&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaGlzdG9yaWMtZGF5LWF0LXRoZS1zdXByZW1lLWNvdXJ0Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=5a554b8227a190207b2dbc5502cb508888486a1ef5653b9571a91e024026b849] in
_Investigative Bulletin _our significant week in court. We look
forward to a decision regarding Election Day that will affect every
voter.

> Judicial Watch was at the Supreme Court on Monday fighting for a
> critical legal determination: Election Day is a day—not five days,
> not a week, not a month.
>
> “This is the most important Supreme Court election integrity case
> in a generation,” said
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37102&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanVkaWNpYWwtd2F0Y2gtc3VwcmVtZS1jb3VydC1icmllZi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=b228433e5e2d34983ed4d9c6cd22e8f3c97279497fbf2b0e1a350c7988cdbdc8]
> Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton. “The pandemic spread of
> states counting late ballots received after Election Day is a
> flagrant violation of long-standing federal law that not only
> encourages voter fraud but also severely undermines public
> confidence in our elections. The Supreme Court now has a critical
> opportunity to restore a fundamental guardrail to the election
> process.”
>
> More than fifteen states allow late-arriving ballots
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37424&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubmNzbC5vcmcvZWxlY3Rpb25zLWFuZC1jYW1wYWlnbnMvdGFibGUtMTEtcmVjZWlwdC1hbmQtcG9zdG1hcmstZGVhZGxpbmVzLWZvci1hYnNlbnRlZS1tYWlsLWJhbGxvdHM/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=3028b3d9b255fd9aa49df13b46f4d835bbc7276c24517e3a132a86d7ac85ab72]
> to be counted. Judicial Watch asked the Supreme Court to uphold a
> ruling by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, which
> struck down as unconstitutional a Mississippi law allowing election
> officials up to five days to count mail-in ballots received after
> Election Day. Mississippi appealed, arguing that late-arriving,
> postmarked ballots were permissible.
>
> The original JW lawsuit, brought on behalf of the Libertarian Party
> of Mississippi, was later consolidated
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37093&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3VwcmVtZWNvdXJ0Lmdvdi9zZWFyY2guYXNweD9maWxlbmFtZT0vZG9ja2V0L2RvY2tldGZpbGVzL2h0bWwvcHVibGljLzI0LTEyNjAuaHRtbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=da4c11666752297155c8f06ad9b76f307bc19bac95f24199ee0897b862e3acdb]
> with a similar challenge by the Republican National Committee and
> others. At the court on Monday, former U.S. Solicitor General Paul
> Clement made the historic opening statement on behalf of Judicial
> Watch’s Libertarian Party client. “All agree that elections for
> federal office have to end on the day of the election specified by
> Congress,” Clement said
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37425&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS90b21maXR0b24vc3RhdHVzLzIwMzYyNDUyOTAxNTY0NDIwMjA/cz00MyZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=eac61d75406e810f1ab56377684b7e7f2ef0b025d00a94940a39d44f15f1a370].
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37425&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS90b21maXR0b24vc3RhdHVzLzIwMzYyNDUyOTAxNTY0NDIwMjA/cz00MyZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=eac61d75406e810f1ab56377684b7e7f2ef0b025d00a94940a39d44f15f1a370]
> “...Nonetheless, Mississippi insists ballots can trickle in days
> or even weeks after Election Day.”
>
> JW’s brief to the Supreme Court
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37089&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3dhdHNvbi12LXJlcHVibGljYW4tbmF0aW9uYWwtY29tbWl0dGVlLXNjb3R1cy1icmllZi0wMDAzNy0xMjYwLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=d6b1274ced4c1855dd698ab8a09a33d45d941248c6e83f6c76cbffdc2c0e8b40]
> makes the case for a single Election Day. There is no historic
> foundation for counting ballots arriving after Election Day, JW
> notes. The opportunities for fraud are endless, and public
> confidence in elections is eroded.
>
> “The whole point of the federal Election-Day statutes is to set a
> single uniform day for the election,” the brief notes. “Allowing
> ballots to trickle in days or weeks after Election Day is
> antithetical to that basic goal.”
>
> Congress set an Election Day, not an Election Week or an Election
> Month. “Through the federal Election-Day statutes, Congress
> exercised its constitutional authority to set a uniform time for
> federal elections to occur. Text, historical practice, precedent,
> and common sense all demonstrate that those statutes set the
> deadline by which ballots must be submitted and received. Simply
> put, the ballot box closes on Election Day, and ballots that are not
> received until days or weeks after the date specified by Congress
> arrive after Election Day and should not be counted.”
>
> It’s been a busy year for Judicial Watch at the Supreme Court. In
> January, the court granted standing
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=36862&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvc3RhdGVtZW50LW9uLXN1cHJlbWUtY291cnQtdmljdG9yeS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=de636c6707638922dd9e766bf7322dceeb9b555f08c46cc6b4e1b808dae9061c]
> in a historic case JW filed on behalf of Congressman Mike Bost and
> two presidential electors. The case challenges an Illinois law
> allowing the counting of ballots received up to fourteen days after
> the election.
>
> The Judicial Watch election integrity team is led by Senior Attorney
> Robert Popper, who previously served in the Voting Section of the
> Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. JW attorneys T.
> Russell Nobile and Eric Lee provide critical support for JW’s many
> landmark legal efforts.
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=35168&F=T&&hash=54a98dc0af766e1e8cc838fce97a5fdf7566055cdbed1702d666a75e847d5956]
>
> On Monday, Tom Fitton reported from outside the Supreme Court
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37426&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9qdWRpY2lhbHdhdGNoL3N0YXR1cy8yMDM2MTUwMDE1NDcxNjMyODgzP3M9NDMmdXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=6e6ce7f6512fabc99c6105f84304c8d9f7066bdaedbac958226c42c30f8daaff] after
> the hearing. The Judicial Watch team had made “historic legal
> arguments to preserve the idea of Election Day,” he said. Court
> observers were largely in agreement that a majority of the justices
> appeared poised to curb late-arriving ballots
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37427&F=T&&hash=3c0705edd6d5e714de2046859d97d3f829bf9ade0beafd622936cdff5eab6632
> predicting what the Supreme Court will do is a fool’s errand. Some
> election officials are not waiting. On Thursday, the New York Times
> reported
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37428&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnl0aW1lcy5jb20vMjAyNi8wMy8yNS91cy9wb2xpdGljcy9zdXByZW1lLWNvdXJ0LW1haWwtYmFsbG90cy1zdGF0ZXMuaHRtbD91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=b32b6cb7150e1397832391404c082e4cd3684e66f44dad9934d71a7631f9435a]
> that election administrators in some states had already begun
> “planning for a world where all ballots must arrive by Election
> Day.”
>
> A decision is expected in June.

ZERO ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED INTO U.S. FOR TENTH CONSECUTIVE MONTH

Here’s some really good news. We are all much safer under President
Trump’s border policies. Our _Corruption Chronicles_ blog has the
details
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37436&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvYm9yZGVyLWZpbmFsbHktc2VjdXJlLXdpdGgtemVyby8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=8c668d41fc192d081dce3734e50764dcaf5bdb88a9621af47b42f4e4e6673d3c].

> Proving that the famous saying coined by the Mexican farm worker
> labor movement of the 1960s—and later adopted by Barack
> Obama—can apply to the once seemingly impossible task of securing
> the border, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) reveals that
> for 10 consecutive months no illegal immigrants
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37441&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY2JwLmdvdi9uZXdzcm9vbS9uYXRpb25hbC1tZWRpYS1yZWxlYXNlL3RlbnRoLXN0cmFpZ2h0LW1vbnRoLXplcm8taWxsZWdhbC1hbGllbnMtcmVsZWFzZWQtYm9yZGVyP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=d46ecf5989d369775f1c3294e4d1ea1894a74cb6cde8d828de400b0c9e8d91aa]
> have been released into the United States. It is cause to celebrate
> considering during the Biden administration a record-breaking 7.6

> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=34595&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdGVycm9yaXN0LXRocmVhdC10by11cy1za3lyb2NrZXRlZC9dZnJvbT91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=13468b27c6973246999bb6c56653fabff87e9519ecb8fe84ed2bf10b88677b03
> countries that DHS determined pose a national security threat to the
> U.S. In about a year the Trump administration has turned it around,
> establishing that, _“Si se puede”_ (yes we can), as the renowned
> labor leader Cesar Chavez, recently exposed
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37442&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnl0aW1lcy5jb20vMjAyNi8wMy8xOC91cy9jZXNhci1jaGF2ZXotc2V4dWFsLWFidXNlLWFsbGVnYXRpb25zLXVmdy5odG1sXWZvcj91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=8f7732f10e576743f8757861d9a7f7cd327b9a3e8b1be7084b761153c438c5a1
> raping and sexually abusing girls and young women in his movement,
> shouted during marches. Decades later Obama adopted
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=80476&L=37443&F=T&&hash=0e9f24ecd55dba1c1ecd836c2dd7b619fbef64676c6eb809863def31e6ef9fb6
> three-word phrase, until then best known as the rallying cry for
> Chavez’s United Farm Workers, as his presidential campaign slogan.
>
> The adage comes to mind because the Biden administration falsely

clean_body: Zero Illegal Aliens Released Into U.S. for Tenth Consecutive Month [INSIDE JW] JUDICIAL WATCH’S HISTORIC DAY AT THE SUPREME COURT [] Our chief investigative reporter, Micah Morrison, recounts [] in Investigative Bulletin our significant week in court. We look forward to a decision regarding Election Day that will affect every voter. Judicial Watch was at the Supreme Court on Monday fighting for a critical legal determination: Election Day is a day—not five days, not a week, not a month. “This is the most important Supreme Court election integrity case in a generation,” said [] Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton. “The pandemic spread of states counting late ballots received after Election Day is a flagrant violation of long-standing federal law that not only encourages voter fraud but also severely undermines public confidence in our elections. The Supreme Court now has a critical opportunity to restore a fundamental guardrail to the election process.” More than fifteen states allow late-arriving ballots [] to be counted. Judicial Watch asked the Supreme Court to uphold a ruling by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, which struck down as unconstitutional a Mississippi law allowing election officials up to five days to count mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Mississippi appealed, arguing that late-arriving, postmarked ballots were permissible. The original JW lawsuit, brought on behalf of the Libertarian Party of Mississippi, was later consolidated [] with a similar challenge by the Republican National Committee and others. At the court on Monday, former U.S. Solicitor General Paul Clement made the historic opening statement on behalf of Judicial Watch’s Libertarian Party client. “All agree that elections for federal office have to end on the day of the election specified by Congress,” Clement said []. [] “...Nonetheless, Mississippi insists ballots can trickle in days or even weeks after Election Day.” JW’s brief to the Supreme Court [] makes the case for a single Election Day. There is no historic foundation for counting ballots arriving after Election Day, JW notes. The opportunities for fraud are endless, and public confidence in elections is eroded. “The whole point of the federal Election-Day statutes is to set a single uniform day for the election,” the brief notes. “Allowing ballots to trickle in days or weeks after Election Day is antithetical to that basic goal.” Congress set an Election Day, not an Election Week or an Election Month. “Through the federal Election-Day statutes, Congress exercised its constitutional authority to set a uniform time for federal elections to occur. Text, historical practice, precedent, and common sense all demonstrate that those statutes set the deadline by which ballots must be submitted and received. Simply put, the ballot box closes on Election Day, and ballots that are not received until days or weeks after the date specified by Congress arrive after Election Day and should not be counted.” It’s been a busy year for Judicial Watch at the Supreme Court. In January, the court granted standing [] in a historic case JW filed on behalf of Congressman Mike Bost and two presidential electors. The case challenges an Illinois law allowing the counting of ballots received up to fourteen days after the election. The Judicial Watch election integrity team is led by Senior Attorney Robert Popper, who previously served in the Voting Section of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. JW attorneys T. Russell Nobile and Eric Lee provide critical support for JW’s many landmark legal efforts. [] On Monday, Tom Fitton reported from outside the Supreme Court [] after the hearing. The Judicial Watch team had made “historic legal arguments to preserve the idea of Election Day,” he said. Court observers were largely in agreement that a majority of the justices appeared poised to curb late-arriving ballots [ predicting what the Supreme Court will do is a fool’s errand. Some election officials are not waiting. On Thursday, the New York Times reported [] that election administrators in some states had already begun “planning for a world where all ballots must arrive by Election Day.” A decision is expected in June. ZERO ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED INTO U.S. FOR TENTH CONSECUTIVE MONTH Here’s some really good news. We are all much safer under President Trump’s border policies. Our Corruption Chronicles blog has the details []. Proving that the famous saying coined by the Mexican farm worker labor movement of the 1960s—and later adopted by Barack Obama—can apply to the once seemingly impossible task of securing the border, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) reveals that for 10 consecutive months no illegal immigrants [] have been released into the United States. It is cause to celebrate considering during the Biden administration a record-breaking 7.6 million illegal aliens entered the country, including hundreds of thousands with serious criminal records and more than 1.7 million [ countries that DHS determined pose a national security threat to the U.S. In about a year the Trump administration has turned it around, establishing that, “Si se puede” (yes we can), as the renowned labor leader Cesar Chavez, recently exposed [ raping and sexually abusing girls and young women in his movement, shouted during marches. Decades later Obama adopted [ three-word phrase, until then best known as the rallying cry for Chavez’s United Farm Workers, as his presidential campaign slogan. The adage comes to mind because the Biden administration falsely claimed the unprecedented influx of illegal immigrants could not be contained as millions fled hardships at home and therefore the border could not be properly secured. The latest figures released by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), the frontline DHS agency, contradict that narrative and demonstrate that federal authorities can indeed secure the once-porous 1,954-mile border we share with Mexico. The records show not only a trend of historically low border crossings but also record high drug seizures. In fact, in February CBP recorded the most drug seizures in more than four years (79,609 pounds), which marks an 84% increase from the previous month. Released just days ago, the statistics go through February. CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott says they are a “clear reflection of the enforcement-first posture restoring integrity to our nation’s borders.” He added that while threats to economic and national security evolve so does the Trump administration’s resolve to meet them. The sustained decline in illegal border crossings and apprehensions is the lowest in over three decades, CBP confirms, demonstrating the impact of robust enforcement policies. Daily apprehensions are down an extraordinary 95% from the Biden administration with 13 consecutive months of fewer than 9,000 southwest border apprehensions, which means the region is more secure than at any point in history. Last month CBP encountered 26,963 illegal immigrants, marking an 88% decline in the monthly average under Biden. Additionally, CBP’s total encounters of 153,155 this fiscal year are 40% lower than just the month of February 2024 under Biden. “The U.S. Border Patrol’s apprehensions along the southwest border in February (6,603) were 92% lower than the monthly average over the last 33 years and 97% below the peak of the Biden administration (December 2023),” the latest DHS figures show. The number of daily Border Patrol apprehensions in February were less than a single hour during the height of the Biden administration when 336 illegal immigrants were arrested per hour in December 2023. This clearly shows “we have the most secure border in American history,” according to CBP. Drug interdictions are also a major part of border security since CBP is responsible for preventing dangerous narcotics from reaching American communities. Under Biden tens of thousands of pounds of illicit drugs flowed over the border []. Under Trump the record February drug seizures include a 129% increase in marijuana, 67% increase in fentanyl, 46% increase in methamphetamine and 39% increase in cocaine seizures over the previous month. Agents also seized 10% more heroin over January. CBP also helped safeguard the American economy by targeting forced labor and counterfeit goods, stopping 266 shipments valued at more than $11 million for potential forced labor violations. Over 440 shipments containing counterfeit goods valued at more than $580 million were also seized and hundreds of civil penalties were issued for undeclared prohibited agriculture items. This is all part of President Trump’s Operation Take Back America [], a nationwide initiative launched last March to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, eliminate drug cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect American communities from perpetrators of violent crime. HAKEEM JEFFRIES’ BROTHER REWRITES HISTORY AT MONTPELIER TO FOCUS ON SLAVERY James Madison, our fourth President, wrote the Bill of Rights and advocated for three branches of government, among many other contributions. But his home at Montpelier has been taken over by radical leftists. Our Corruption Chronicles blog reports []. Though President Trump is restoring federal sites dedicated to history back to promoting American pride and unity over woke ideological indoctrination, equally important historical landmarks operated privately by radical leftists continue to alter U.S history with critical race narratives that downplay the significant contributions of the nation’s founders. As the country’s 250th anniversary approaches this deserves to be reported, especially because one of the sites managed—and heavily impacted—by the left is James Madison’s Montpelier, the 2,650-acre property in northwestern Virginia that was home to the “Father of the Constitution” and fourth president of the United States. Rather than focus on Madison’s many accomplishments and multitude of political contributions—such as shaping the Constitution and the country—most of the Montpelier exhibits are centered on slavery and its “central role in framing of the nation” as well as its “lasting legacies,” an extensive report [] [ by the Heritage Foundation a few years ago reveals. This is disgraceful and despite its historical significance Montpelier is not impacted by Trump’s 2025 executive order [] to reverse a yearslong “effort to rewrite our Nation’s history, replacing objective facts with a distorted narrative driven by ideology rather than truth” at national parks, museums, monuments and memorials. Montpelier is a casualty of what the president’s order identifies as a “revisionist movement to undermine the remarkable achievements of the United States by casting its founding principles and historical milestones in a negative light.” Under the historical revision America’s unparalleled legacy of advancing liberty, individual rights, and human happiness is reconstructed as inherently racist, sexist, oppressive, or otherwise irredeemably flawed. At Montpelier Madison’s legacy “has been effectively erased, as there are no exhibits dedicated to his significant contributions,” the comprehensive probe conducted by the conservative Washington D.C. think tank found. “Montpelier can now be counted among the ranks of projects and actors that promote a distorted view of American history, suffused with critical race theory (CRT).” Madison’s signal contributions to the founding of America are seriously downplayed and there is no genuine focus on Madison the political philosopher and statesman or written displays dedicated to his many acts of public service. His drafting of the Bill of Rights is barely mentioned and with few small exceptions all the galleries and exhibits at Montpelier focus on slavery and Jim Crow. “The visitor is left with the impression that slavery was the central animating force behind the laws and economy of the United States,” the Heritage report concludes, adding that there is a palpable lack of education about Madison’s ideas and contributions to the American Republic. The woke transformation occurred because the radical left, including the Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) which features conservative organizations on a catalogue of “hate groups,” is running the historical site. The chairman of the Montpelier Foundation that operates the landmark is Hasan Kwane Jeffries [], brother of New York Democratic Congressman Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader. Hasan teaches courses on Black Power Movement and civil rights at Ohio State University and consults regularly with school districts on developing anti-racism programming, according to his biography []. His areas of expertise include African American history, race, ethnicity, power and culture and he helped the SPLC develop a history framework for elementary and high schools that claims, “slavery is our country’s origin.” Hasan also hosts a podcast produced by the SPLC, a leftwing nonprofit that labels legitimate groups that disagree with it on social issues hateful. In 2013 a domestic terrorist who carried out a politically motivated shooting [] [ the Family Research Council, a pro-life nonprofit, got his target list from the SPLC catalogue of “hate groups.” The Montpelier Foundation’s vice chair, Leslie Alexander, is a specialist in early African American and African Diaspora history who is responsible for a project called “How We Got Here: Slavery and the Making of the Modern Police State,” [] which examines how surveillance of free and enslaved black communities in the colonial and antebellum eras laid the foundation for policing today. “Despite growing public awareness that mass incarceration has its roots in slavery, and that racial bias infects all aspects of our criminal justice system, our nation has yet to reckon with the reality that contemporary systems of policing and mass criminalization have powerful, significant histories that originated in white fear—not merely of Black people, but also of Black resistance and the very notion of Black freedom,” Alexander claims. Her research appears in the 1619 Project [], a highly controversial initiative launched by a mainstream newspaper that aims to reframe the country’s history by placing slavery and anti-black racism at the center of the national narrative, asserting that they are foundational to the institutions of the United States. A key figure in the 1619 Project, civil rights journalist Nikole Hannah-Jones, has also falsely depicted the American Revolution as a pro-slavery cause. U.S. INVESTS $1.5 MILLION IN MEXICAN PARTNERSHIP AFTER SIMILAR PROJECT FAILED If at first you don’t succeed, throw more money at it. That seems to be our State Department’s strategy, as our Corruption Chronicles blog reports []. Despite the failure of a multi-billion-dollar endeavor to combat transnational crime, drug trafficking and money laundering by partnering with notoriously corrupt law enforcement agencies in Mexico the United States is investing more money in a similar program in the hopes of creating a more solid partnership with the poorly qualified Mexican institutions. Much like the last delusional project—known as the Merida Initiative—the goal is to fight organized crime and violence by improving the effectiveness of frontline police and prosecutors in Mexico through the elimination of “critical gaps” in key areas that impact the success of detentions, seizures and prosecutions. This includes enhancing basic law enforcement procedures such as the handling of evidence, report writing and legal interoperability, according to a grant announcement [] issued this month by the State Department’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs. Up to $1.5 million will be spent on the new Mexican partnership, which also aims to teach special unit officers in the Latin American nation run by drug cartels to consistently document evidence in accordance with legal standards and to regularly conduct joint investigations that disrupt transnational criminal networks with their U.S. counterparts. The American taxpayer funds will also help train Mexican prosecutors to consistently prepare charges that align with criminal law standards, organize evidence for effective court proceedings and collaborate with U.S. law enforcement counterparts to support cross-border investigations and prosecutions. The State Department claims the project will advance U.S. national interests and directly support the security of the United States since it will “enhance Mexico’s ability to combat cartel-related crime, reduce impunity, and disrupt transnational criminal networks that threaten U.S. and regional security.” The effort reflects the America First commitment to “strategic partnerships that deliver concrete results for the American people while advancing mutual security interests with Mexico,” according to the grant document. Since the mid-2000s Uncle Sam has given Mexico billions of dollars in security and counternarcotics assistance as record amounts of drugs, including methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine and other illicit narcotics enter the country through the southern border and cartel violence spills into American communities in the region. Most of the money flowed through the futile Merida Initiative [], a costly partnership between the U.S. and Mexico to fight organized crime and associated violence by, among other things, training police, investigators, prosecutors and implementing justice sector reforms in Mexico’s unreliable system. Congress appropriated $2.5 billion for the Merida Initiative, which also paid for basic law enforcement courses for Mexican police such as crime investigation, criminal intelligence, tactics and firearms, forensics, and training to combat gangs, human trafficking, money laundering and kidnapping. Anti-corruption courses were also handsomely funded under the Merida Initiative, which ran from 2008 to 2021 and barely put a dent on the cartel drug-trafficking crisis. In a report [] published in the fall of 2021, the Congressional Research Service (CRS) wrote that “escalating violence in Mexico and drug overdose deaths in the United States have led many to question the Mérida Initiative’s overall efficacy.” The CRS, which conducts official research for Congress, also found that “impunity for public corruption continues in Mexico.” Which brings us to this month’s $1.5 million allocation to improve the effectiveness of Mexican law enforcement, an effort that is unlikely to thrive considering the U.S. has already poured a lot of money into the cause with little success. In fact, a federal audit [] released to the public in 2021 determined that Merida Initiative funds were provided to individuals and organizations involved in contract fraud, human rights abuses, drug trafficking and other crimes. The State Department never bothered to assess the potential risks of fraud in its Merida programs, according to the probe conducted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the investigative arm of Congress. This month’s grant document states the obvious; that Mexican law enforcement and prosecutorial units face complex challenges in combating organized crime, particularly cartel activity. Resource constraints and the need for professional development present the U.S. with “ongoing opportunities” to strengthen our southern neighbor’s legal and investigative processes, the State Department writes, omitting that we have tried in vain before and it cost American taxpayers billions of dollars. body:
Dear Hoosier Republicans, No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-dj/) _**Moving Forward**_ Dear Hoosier Republicans,In 2026, I am proud to say that Hoosiers have a lot to be optimistic about. Our economy is growing, job opportunities are expanding, communities are safer, our leaders have put affordability front and center, and Hoosier families are keeping more of what they earn. Indiana is moving forward, and these are the results we have fought for.But none of this progress is guaranteed. The choices we make this year will determine whether Indiana continues to grow, protect families, and safeguard opportunity, or whether the gains we've fought for are eroded and reversed. Now is the time to step up, volunteer, knock doors, make calls, and show up at the polls, because the future of Indiana depends on the energy, dedication, and action of every Hoosier who cares about keeping our state strong. As always, thank you for being a part of our team, and please feel free to reach out if there's any way I can be of assistance.Yours in service, Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman _**Governor Braun Praises IURC for Strong Defense of Ratepayers Following Utility Hearing, Expresses Disappointment with Utilities ' Defense of High Rates**_ Following the March 24 utility rate hearing, Governor Mike Braun praised the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission and Chairman Andy Zay for pressing utilities on rising costs. Pointing to the largest climb in residential electric rates in the Midwest, up 28.9% since 2014, Governor Braun insists that Hoosiers need relief. "I will personally review the results of Tuesday's hearing and the full listening sessions to identify every additional way we can deliver real relief to ratepayers. With HEA 1002 now law, we have the tools to make it happen, and these sessions will ensure the voices of the people paying the bills come first."\- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-r/) **_Governor Braun Invests in Public Safety, Delivers Long-Overdue Justice_** Governor Mike Braun has boosted funding for the Indiana State Police Forensic Laboratory by more than $3 million, while streamlining operations and reducing administration costs. These targeted investments and reforms have driven a 19% reduction in the DNA backlog and a 50% increase in processing capacity, helping to solve decades-old cold cases."For too long, families have waited for answers. We made smart investments in technology and cut red tape so our State Police can do their jobs more effectively. The results speak for themselves - criminals are being held accountable, no matter how much time has passed, and Hoosiers are safer because of it." \- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-y/) _**Chairwoman's County Visits: 12**_ **Fulton County** **Martin County** **Boone County** _**Emerging Republican Leaders**_ **Grant Bailey** Grant Bailey is a student at Rochester High School, an intern for Mayor Trent Odell, and an active member of the Fulton County GOP. Grant's eagerness to step up, serve his community, and engage in the political process has been a welcome asset to his county party and a model example of the next generation of conservative leadership. **2026 State Convention** [Click Here for More Information](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-j/) [Individual Registration](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-t/) [Organization Registration](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-i/) [Guest (Non-Delegate) Registration](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-d/) _**Indiana GOP is Hiring Interns for the Spring & Summer**_ **📱 _News You Can Use_ ** **Governor Mike Braun**** **[highlighted](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-h/) the decisive action his administration has taken on healthcare, saying, "We are protecting patients from unfair medical debt collection, requiring hospitals to connect patients with payment assistance before sending bills to collections, and strengthening the pipeline of future doctors serving rural Indiana. These are concrete steps to fix the broken health care system making it harder for Hoosiers to make ends meet at the kitchen table."**Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith** [spoke](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-k/) at Purdue University Northwest with Turning Point USA, engaging with students on issues like energy, infrastructure, and taxes. Beckwith praised the event's organization and highlighted the thoughtful questions from students.**Secretary Diego Morales **[announced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-b/) the launch of a new system designed to make it easier for military and overseas Hoosiers to register, request, and track absentee ballots. The secure platform aims to improve accessibility while maintaining the integrity of Indiana's election process.**Treasurer Daniel Elliott **[recognized](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-n/) National Ag Day, celebrating Indiana's farmers and the vital role agriculture plays across the state.**Attorney General Todd Rokita **[co-led](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-p/) a multi-state brief opposing court-ordered sex-change surgeries for prisoners, arguing the Eighth Amendment does not require states to provide such procedures. Rokita said the case could have nationwide implications for state authority over prison healthcare and taxpayer costs.**Senator Todd Young **[led](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-x/) a letter urging the Trump Administration to reinstate the Protect Life Rule, which would prevent federal Title X funds from being used for abortions or abortion referrals. Young said the effort is aimed at ensuring taxpayer dollars are not used to fund abortion services.**Senator Jim Banks **[spoke](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-m/) at the Hill and Valley Forum on the global AI competition with China, emphasizing the need for stronger export controls and U.S. leadership in advanced technology. Banks described the AI race as both a national security and moral issue, highlighting efforts like his GAIN AI Act to limit adversaries' access to critical technology.**Congressman Rudy Yakym **[supported](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-c/) five bipartisan tax relief bills advanced by the Ways and Means Committee, aimed at providing targeted relief for taxpayers, including disaster victims, educators, and survivors of abuse. Yakym said the legislation is focused on making the tax code fairer, more transparent, and more responsive to everyday Americans.**Congressman Marlin Stutzman **[introduced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-q/) legislation to study potential reforms to the nation's deposit insurance system, directing federal agencies to evaluate whether coverage levels should be increased. The bill aims to strengthen financial stability and ensure banks and credit unions can continue serving communities effectively.**Congressman Jim Baird **[testified](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-a/) before the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, highlighting priorities including support for agricultural research programs and careful consideration of hemp policy changes.**Congresswoman Victoria Spartz **[announced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-f/) a series of live policy discussions on X Spaces beginning in April, covering major issues such as national debt, surveillance, and health care. The events will be held twice a month and include guest speakers and audience participation.**Congressman Jefferson Shreve **[met](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-z/) with student government leaders from Indiana University Bloomington to discuss key issues and student priorities. Shreve praised the group's engagement and interest in making an impact on campus and beyond.**Congressman Mark Messmer **[praised](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-e/) a $200 million investment by Toyota in its Gibson County facility, highlighting the expansion's impact on job growth and manufacturing in Southwest Indiana. Messmer said the investment reflects strong economic momentum and supports continued opportunities for Hoosier workers.**Congresswoman Erin Houchin** [issued](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-adlkthl-hhlljjcji-s/) a joint statement calling for stronger federal action to protect children online following a verdict involving social media companies. Houchin emphasized the need for bipartisan legislation to establish age requirements and hold platforms accountable for user safety. **_Upcoming Events_****March 29: [Fountain County Lincoln Day clean_body: Dear Hoosier Republicans, No images? Moving Forward Dear Hoosier Republicans,In 2026, I am proud to say that Hoosiers have a lot to be optimistic about. Our economy is growing, job opportunities are expanding, communities are safer, our leaders have put affordability front and center, and Hoosier families are keeping more of what they earn. Indiana is moving forward, and these are the results we have fought for.But none of this progress is guaranteed. The choices we make this year will determine whether Indiana continues to grow, protect families, and safeguard opportunity, or whether the gains we've fought for are eroded and reversed. Now is the time to step up, volunteer, knock doors, make calls, and show up at the polls, because the future of Indiana depends on the energy, dedication, and action of every Hoosier who cares about keeping our state strong. As always, thank you for being a part of our team, and please feel free to reach out if there's any way I can be of assistance.Yours in service, Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman Governor Braun Praises IURC for Strong Defense of Ratepayers Following Utility Hearing, Expresses Disappointment with Utilities ' Defense of High Rates Following the March 24 utility rate hearing, Governor Mike Braun praised the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission and Chairman Andy Zay for pressing utilities on rising costs. Pointing to the largest climb in residential electric rates in the Midwest, up 28.9% since 2014, Governor Braun insists that Hoosiers need relief. "I will personally review the results of Tuesday's hearing and the full listening sessions to identify every additional way we can deliver real relief to ratepayers. With HEA 1002 now law, we have the tools to make it happen, and these sessions will ensure the voices of the people paying the bills come first."\- Governor Braun via a Governor Braun Invests in Public Safety, Delivers Long-Overdue Justice Governor Mike Braun has boosted funding for the Indiana State Police Forensic Laboratory by more than $3 million, while streamlining operations and reducing administration costs. These targeted investments and reforms have driven a 19% reduction in the DNA backlog and a 50% increase in processing capacity, helping to solve decades-old cold cases."For too long, families have waited for answers. We made smart investments in technology and cut red tape so our State Police can do their jobs more effectively. The results speak for themselves - criminals are being held accountable, no matter how much time has passed, and Hoosiers are safer because of it." \- Governor Braun via a Chairwoman's County Visits: 12 Fulton County Martin County Boone County Emerging Republican Leaders Grant Bailey Grant Bailey is a student at Rochester High School, an intern for Mayor Trent Odell, and an active member of the Fulton County GOP. These are concrete steps to fix the broken health care system making it harder for Hoosiers to make ends meet at the kitchen table."Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith at Purdue University Northwest with Turning Point USA, engaging with students on issues like energy, infrastructure, and taxes. Beckwith praised the event's organization and highlighted the thoughtful questions from students.Secretary Diego Morales the launch of a new system designed to make it easier for military and overseas Hoosiers to register, request, and track absentee ballots. Rokita said the case could have nationwide implications for state authority over prison healthcare and taxpayer costs.Senator Todd Young a letter urging the Trump Administration to reinstate the Protect Life Rule, which would prevent federal Title X funds from being used for abortions or abortion referrals. But a loss hands MAGA a comeback path, setting them up to flip the court just months before the 2028 presidential election.
We all know how that works. The presidency comes down to a handful of swing states. Wisconsin is always on that list. MAGA with a court in their pocket doesn't just tilt the playing field. It hands them the keys to the whole state.
There has only been one poll on this race, and it shows that the vast majority of voters are undecided. Democrats are building a nationwide redistricting movement that could blow up Trump's entire election rigging scheme.

Their proposal creates an alternative redistricting process that voters would have no meaningful control over, one designed specifically to make sure Colorado never becomes a threat to MAGA's gerrymandered maps.
This changes everything.
What was a clear path to the ballot is now a two-front war. We still need to collect 200,000 signatures to get our initiative in front of voters. But now we also have to mount an offensive to keep their poison pill proposal off the ballot entirely.
If both initiatives make it to voters, MAGA wins by confusion. They don't need to beat us outright. They just need to muddy the waters enough that nothing passes.

## House Rejects Senate Bill to Partly Fund DHS
House Speaker Mike Johnson on Friday [rejected a Senate-passed bill](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMR2RvRiMCxfX0P3XXokcvOCNjB3hJVHe_kRe4e9GGumTZv79zD-eEuXtr9_R8VrmjO-akBmPOZaz4oEPXLhWzJ7xTikxbTNIGFrZtTDOwVP6zLoJbkUE7Bp0yhg9WOgtNNFJv4bBhh69AaWMxdX0oBC1CuMyLr4hd2myg1FJabW9GWONkUrppcduvFuhJQbictwehTJHXNOnvPC4LWVvkovMzyq6PwImARNHjJTS1QmYYtnxGvSNZ0UBUz9K3eu-rfHkUN65XWmL3F5gG2Jt1zMHypuAqTlceL4pJaqDEVpuu6cv3PCvnno5-B8AAP__-9h9Hg) to fund much of the Department of Homeland Security, calling the measure "a joke," and instead proposing an eight-week stopgap to fund the entire department, leaving the partial government shutdown in place. The rebuke of the upper chamber came just hours after the Senate voted early Friday morning, at 2:20 a.m., [to fund most of DHS, including TSA,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAQRL8GOiOzGAyFizR0L21KZOwF9snXRvbei_j7iOQTXjfSSKM558_X8mUpUNx_2xca3tIS8SoBmTEvR3oXzPiNjkvBaBlXCoFpX0DCIGQnYFy8pXAvqvZmQwTsajSt1mqYoJ-gPoweh05KJeU4wKoAQfpp3SR477rejVtN5lmTHYytlJOaGq0nrWXbKtdjN65TpSR64pSb70SRD9zCnT6YG5dedTAH81mq7lcFcwXzdV1NXN1D8fQVzGcKxORKBbNLcc9YnvifR9g9IxaxvaMX_iiCHIo1ZY9ZnJZzCmIlL8rxZp-uKLhYcdpbeAz2LiK7aGHoWznW2fjzohCoDLpScn9ZCv8O8o-sfgz8DQAA___7q42e) the Coast Guard, and FEMA, while stripping out funding for ICE and border security operations. The bill was approved by the Senate Friday as President Trump signed a presidential memorandum to [begin paying TSA agents](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8GNiL8wMYMDF28pWtHC5tn8yJsIkMS5e8rt1J_oPO9OtI5X9fx6inRvn76DV1d8rjjqySsFY8x5kfBA28411Jw9xUnSqnSOoKETkgloB-Dp_QeNQ9uQQRUHF1jjO4stBZ4dAr94icfurnvZmggoIZFBcRWT5MNnpM7aVJB30hptb0YY42RTaPnFlU_WaYlBqr5uNwy7TXikt75icdlzhtPLtZ6L0x9MBgYDDVipJTOjcEQ84anEIPhV4DB0PZSGTCiFi9CLGJ57IH2VdCM4u_EDxfuL0qJSmeYluvm6QfK678qPR18BwAA__-ymXwJ) who are working without pay, with some airports seeing TSA absentee rates up to 40%. Johnson said he intended to hold a separate vote "as soon as possible" on a continuing resolution to fund all of DHS, including ICE and border security, through May 22.
## Iran Hackers Publish FBI Director's Emails
An Iran-linked hacking group called Handala published over 300 emails and photos Friday [from FBI Director Kash Patel's personal email account](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupSAURb8GOwwiihQU09i9aac0CEfhvXPRwLnX-PcT5xem3tk7e60_X8uXS5jy_tu9wNJ2LBmuikAEZYnHu0KBb_BUK2RHsCZESvsihRy56LmcluAS3otqgt0AJPQN2E5rNRo5GNlEG0Q3hFF4PwwTmE15MflVr73qgoDQqybZZ030cuqEMMq0WhutRdcpP0A_rYYpASHRUdrvI2WKsOF9fKC0_ng1aCPRWVn_i8mZyfm6rjav_qF4ciZnAh-ZnCv4d0l0Mzmn4nJymUfnf6BUfr5XTDVyeLmElTtE2CHgzSsdCJn_uBr56QiQF5-dHAdlRFNsOK-EmOqomRL7U_53if7L48fKvwEAAP__CMqJKQ), in what the group called retaliation for the U.S. seizing its websites. The FBI acknowledged the breach, stating it had taken steps to mitigate risks. The bureau said the [compromised information was historical](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdEb22uC4cPE3dPnbK5ExS9jEgcjeC8rbn7hXuG6kGc1ovq_reI2Uabv9j08MvOzjhkfNyIxlXPfvigXvmLhW3CLjRDkz3UZQ0EtlJFzGOVL-jLaZw4IIaBoM2jnbe-g8NGtwunPaepeU0h3YNPcxTcYabXrjNZiGwtmmDFy0Ut761jnvnNLapg7NZfLCKpyJ99Led9p4xSV_9jeWNu3PJoeV-VWF-SdgEDAcx9GmqZ4vTl_AcEoBwzKRnKlg4r3IR6yrfEXGLPEZKcs1pgeWKnOJm4ChKWF-HZQz1d4Jq25n6HeP_wTpHeAnAAD__46-euU) and contained no government data. The leaked emails date mostly from 2010 to 2022 and include personal and family correspondence. Cybersecurity experts told NBC News the hackers likely obtained the material well before releasing it, waiting for a strategic moment. The Justice Department has accused Handala of operating as a front for Iran's Ministry of Intelligence. The State Department has offered up to $10 million for information identifying the group's members.
## Map: Where State Income Taxes Hit Hardest
A [new map of state income tax rates](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAURp9GOwwCihQU29jNtluaK171TlAM3Bl33n4z-wp__-U7J-fPY3oARTq333Cg5zVNJ94lIjPmaU-vghmfGLgUPIFxphiZtklJ1QuphRqmBSh-JlMvfkVUqGv0rbWmd6pzqt49otOqm7vV6tC6eTC6M8OwGGgh9HLoavLfN6nV0ErpjGusddbKtjWhQz3MrjISF-KUm2eik3dc4ye9MTchHXX0O_NVKv2rUmOlxvu-mzeVF8QAFzFEKvwdVmrkdIkD8kYnREFnSAcKhr8iA2MR80cUBkbxtanUWGe_XDfFSKW3lZHbART_I_lHnd5e_QsAAP__DaB8yw) reveals a wide divide between where top earners keep the most and least of their paychecks. California leads the nation with a top marginal rate of 13.3%, followed by Hawaii (11.0%) and New York (10.9%), while nine states, including Texas and Florida, [charge no income tax at all](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OrDAQBk9jMpBpjI0DBy8hm5duiBpowCNjj-yev9uvZqU9wUZf9lWpvi7TBX3wcf-PJzne0hTpWQIxU56OdC-U6UoLl0IRmWYfAvt9Agm6ll0Nw7SiD-9JVavbiIC6ilxrjNIWegvV4QBxaakdUBKgnFXfd9tiO6m1Hsw868q7z5vsYGiltMo2xlhjZNuqpadumK1QklbPKTfX5CMftIV3elBulnRWwR3MtyK6fwJGASPja0v3uCL7FJuUdwHjiowCRgxBwFgYmX639nFJJ9WMrzojU6k_LgLGKrv19vQh-KKNUHI_0YcfIP-p0sPBdwAAAP__rb57FA). Coastal states and the Northeast dominate the high end, while Sun Belt and Mountain West states cluster at the bottom. Several states are actively cutting rates, with 26 having reduced individual income tax rates since 2021 and Mississippi targeting full elimination by 2040. [See the full map here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAURp9GOwwCihQU29jNtluaK171TlAM3Bl33n4z-wp__-U7J-fPY3oARTq333Cg5zVNJ94lIjPmaU-vghmfGLgUPIFxphiZtklJ1QuphRqmBSh-JlMvfkVUqGv0rbWmd6pzqt49otOqm7vV6tC6eTC6M8OwGGgh9HLoavLfN6nV0ErpjGusddbKtjWhQz3MrjISF-KUm2eik3dc4ye9MTchHXX0O_NVKv2rUmOlxvu-mzeVF8QAFzFEKvwdVmrkdIkD8kYnREFnSAcKhr8iA2MR80cUBkbxtanUWGe_XDfFSKW3lZHbART_I_lHnd5e_QsAAP__DaB8yw).

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. ## $16 Billion Natural Gas Hub Headed to East Texas
Anderson County in rural East Texas will soon be home to a [$16 billion natural gas-fired power facility](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGOpDAQRL8Gska2MQYCgkvI9tILUdtug3Uee2R6lt2_PzH3CRu2WqqqV_XnY_vAmGLef-ODFv4KZct0nYmYqW6EJzN94fksF9XjZZkon1xxU0IZED2oafMY0_emW79Y4WfZ0iLHUZt5GJVoj8XTQKEXSprBOIOj1Rhmo6U2gqTS1MblFhO9mqQUcpg6HMMUyFnywYTRyEYL8pFL7figd5yQvssn1c6VR5uWg_l5Nv2vRq2NWq_r6v4y5fvZqPWmadR6MjL9P0EaCxn5VTHBjifslKkix5LheFmwFPMO9hUTQ8xwdwBvV_DICI4yUwUuEEpK5WrUipWjS7TNPU3BEYEYfIBBuhksCgdm9M54LYbJTN3Bj9TWxT-vmFI8zdhosT8wpjcN_2yDz0X9CwAA__8N3Z1g), the Texas Power Generation Hub, built and operated by NextEra Energy Resources. The plant will generate up to 5.2 gigawatts of electricity--enough [to power more than one million Texas homes](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOpSAUhZ9GO04AL2hBMY3dP-2UZgMbJYNgYHsubz_xvMLU61srX9afn_UHQgxp-w0Hanr7vCZ81YhEWFaESoRvqGd-YdkvQ4ipUoFVcjky3jE5rQ5C_Kx967ThbhYtaqFUP86DkrzdtTOyB5DCeD-Bd0LZuRfjNHSDm52Stg36HuOdnITgYpgeoPzk0Rp0fvRqFE3P0QXK5UE7fnV8_OQnlofNRxv1TnTWpvvVyKWRyxeoNhe0UNyNNHKJ2UK8w3IdJzNg_6JjYmQmxBhyYgnoKhDZBpXtl2E2HyFtjDKD5LDUnJjNV6JPI5e2aHe-7mIdVdPz7YAQvyr0fwc-tfwXAAD__4YpiP4). The project is part of a $550 billion U.S.-Japan investment agreement signed last October between President Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. State Rep. Cody Harris (R-Palestine), who was at the White House for the announcement, said the hub will bring 3,000 high-paying jobs and help cut local property taxes. The news comes amid growing bipartisan concern over data center expansion across rural Texas, with lawmakers on both sides warning of strain on local water and power resources.
## ** ** House Speaker Eyes Annexing Part of New Mexico
Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows has directed the [Select Committee on Governmental Oversight](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSoyAUhZ8GOx1EAS0otrHLtls6F7lEZhEyeBPM2_-TvMJfnznnfPP9u603CDGk-1840NDl85qwnhGJsKwIJxFecD5yxbI_LSGmkwqsggvV8qEV0-ogxPc6Ns5Y7ua-QdNrPapZasGb3UjvB2flIL1AK2Zp7ewn0KMclMdRQhPMZ4wPYup73supA-0nj5tF55XXqmcjRxcol452_OL4-M4vLN2WjyaanehxsuEPEwsTS621-5-BPiETCxQKW0Qmlm-zTVjbA6-w5dbm4rC0W34mCni2kBJeQCEnJhbNJ6UGKZti3KOGGMOpNBv5_YAQv8f0O10vI34CAAD__71egXQ) to study the feasibility of adding one or more New Mexico counties along the state line to Texas.

The focus is on Lea County, an oil-rich slice of the Permian Basin that Burrows says deserves "a real voice in its own future, not one dictated by Santa Fe." The idea got a [cold reception in New Mexico](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ypCAQRp8GM6YQf9CAYBOzu-mGViOtUoPgQs_Fefstp_YNbtx1Tp3-_nzNX-C8C9tvOFDTtcY5YMkeiTDNCJkIL8hnLJj2lyHEkCnBLIXsuWi4HGYLzr_ntrLaCDvWFepaqbYfOyVFtWsjoV_BjrYdAaXtO6NMY6xRQ9e20KnK6VsmGjnUtai74QFqHVZcDNq1X1Vfs1agdRTTg3b85Kz-Hb8xPZZ4VF7vRGdmzS8mJyanUsrjmf7ifWRyur9hcjqjd-SWzLcbDAcGYnL6yPgeXxl5PhGemHiBQJlnAkJOkfsYn9wFihxCwMuFjQcs_MDLLZEv8RXIYeYx_Ee8C8jkVCVtz-K8d7lXrBXbAc5_eulnK39r-S8AAP__TYOX1A), where Democrats control the legislature and the governor's office. New Mexico House Speaker Javier Martinez fired back, telling Burrows to "get offline, touch some grass, and get his own House in order." The annexation push is one of Burrows' stated priorities heading into the 2027 legislative session. A similar proposal introduced in New Mexico's recent session never made it out of committee.

### Read to the bottom for a special message from Mo the cat 🐱🐾
Mar 28
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..0u4TU3EW4t9pviSjv2VhpJwPM7ZCCt3e35uqrLTMDIo?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

---

Folks,
Here's where things stand as we approach the end of the first quarter of 2026:
Poll after poll has shown Haley statistically tied with our MAGA opponent, Mike Rogers. She's polling way ahead of her primary opponents with independent voters, and there's no doubt now that she's the only Democrat who can win this race.
**She has the momentum to win this race, and our opponents are taking notice.**
Donald Trump and JD Vance have already made visits to Michigan because they're scared of the grassroots movement we're building here.
They're going all-out trying to convince Michiganders that Mike Rogers is one of us instead of a rich MAGA minion being shipped in from Florida to provide another vote for Trump's disastrous agenda.
And meanwhile, the GOP is ramping up their spending here, pouring millions of dollars in outside money into this race so they can flood the airwaves in an attempt to drown us out.
Elon Musk, the Koch network, and their far-right billionaire buddies are trying to buy this seat for Rogers and if we're not careful, that's exactly what they're going to do.
**That 's why our upcoming end-of-quarter deadline is so important. **This is the first big FEC deadline of the election year, and soon, all our numbers will be public.
That means everyone - including our opponents - will be able to see what this campaign has raised so far this year, and they'll be using those numbers to judge whether we have the resources to compete.
A strong FEC report will confirm what the polling numbers show and prove what we've been saying all along: That this team has what it takes to win.
**We 've crunched the numbers, and in order to make the best showing possible, we need to raise another $500,000 before the FEC deadline hits. We only have until midnight on Tuesday to reach our goal, and we're counting on folks like you to help us get there.**
**[If you're able, will you rush an end-of-quarter donation now to help us meet our $500,000 goal, put out a strong FEC report, and win in Michigan?](https://substack.com/redirect/045d28b9-d361-4c59-96f0-a211c76ad4ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/045d28b9-d361-4c59-96f0-a211c76ad4ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for being a part of this team,
Sam
_Haley 's Campaign Manager_
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a87e7e00-004b-4276-ad74-f56ae328e168?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Meooooow, Mo here:

I don't usually involve myself in the affairs of the humans, but my human, Sam, is Haley's Campaign Manager, and with this big deadline coming up, he's been so busy that he hasn't even noticed all the stuff I've knocked off the shelf.

I've tried everything - blocking his camera during Zoom calls, sitting on his laptop, even screaming from the next room over... and normally, my human drops everything for me when I do that, so this is serious.

And it's all because the humans need to reach their $500,000 end-of-quarter goal. Once they do, Sam will put all the books back on the shelf so that I can knock them down again. This is important, so please:

Will you make this the purrrfect day for me (and Team Haley) by donating whatever you can now? I wouldn't ask if this wasn't extremely important.

subject: I’m asking
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Peter, I don’t do this nearly enough. So, before anything else, I want to thank you for your support.
I am no fan of having to send out these emails and text messages. Sometimes I have a hard time wrapping my head around the idea that people actually contribute in response to them.
But hundreds of thousands of people have — and there's no telling what the outcome of my previous races may have been if they ignored messages like this.
Today, I am asking you to join them. Here's why:
The outcome of this election will determine whether we are able to put a check on President Trump during the final two years of his term. We have to take back the House and the Senate.
Taking those majorities back could depend almost entirely on Arizona, where we’ve got a few red-to-blue House races that everybody is looking at. And I am also being asked to travel to help elect Democrats in red and purple places that Donald Trump won, and where I know we can flip.
All that takes resources, so I am asking people who care to step up and help as the election heats up.

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

TODAY is No Kings Day – and together we're going to make it the biggest,
boldest show of resistance yet.

Across cities, small towns, and everywhere in between, over 3,000 No Kings
events are happening to send Trump a clear message: he is NOT King – and
the power STILL belongs to the people.

Today could be the biggest single day of protest in history, but we need
EVERYONE to turnout. Will you join us?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36197?t=1011&akid=10446%2E5885482%2E_y03wG ]Yes, I’m In!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36197?t=1012&akid=10446%2E5885482%2E_y03wG ]FIND AN EVENT

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36197?t=1013&akid=10446%2E5885482%2E_y03wG ]No Kings event map

In June, over 5 million of us came together at more than 2,000 No Kings
Day actions. Then, in October, 7 MILLION people joined in at more than
2,700 events across the country.

Since then, Trump has only gotten more dangerous – sending armed forces
into our cities, starting another endless war against Iran, and coming
after anyone who dares to stand up to his authoritarianism.

Together we can shatter records to make this the biggest day of protest in
U.S. history. But that depends on ALL of us showing up, sending a clear
message to Trump and the rest of the world that our country rejects
authoritarianism – and we're ready to stand up for democracy, for our
neighbors, for a future we build together.

Our Revolution was born from the idea that power belongs to us – not the
billionaires or wannabe dictators. TODAY, we will come together in

and support they need to make today a success.

Thank you for all that you do – and see you in the streets, or standing
strong with us in spirit!

When we organize, we win,

Our Revolution

It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.
I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you.
I promise to always stand between you and the Democrat Machine that aims to obliterate everything that makes our country great.
[Which brings me to the purpose of my email today.](http://links.maga-conservatives.com/u/click?_t=da215d85003f407c964bf56cae76557f&_m=a3c55197f3ea4c9787290474c91648a2&_e=yM-Qizn4TtmJyNLJQczr4grhvBRBjr3Ab1pCmK40nYDdpqKPppOuvsEkutKtreJhn0AqQd6Od9gBhc0Qw2UC7CEWdsit0oLv1dfst0waPiIIEu82DfSseZ27qHn1HX_pqIG9vbB0cN7b-sO4pRUSPpDt6TdJ_LKCY0ZozixyNmzXfuBMjdqGK6PqAfK3ZPBj1WZNAkBlgEZa3Udcvua5N4Q_sdihKFh4BZx7x26Qba6wcXmKCCSZDHoXwvj8MEeftddQ9dntW2hXxuX0HbfeVztga5XtxRMgOhnUGkKBwO5lanEExvWeKkFIMANbl_sgGyk97mEzu4evUpNw7H7_3_IHGqRyir_FW_bx9W_b7PkiJwDxpivdyS8yl2omNmv6eHAImENZ51FNULHvVa2YO7SRKKHpY3NBrAqQgmxCuQg6gGvSjdevOZYwN2RKqGms180nuMDFqJSFVu4VnVVbajjuMqgYctnrjzYMeLd7m0i4bV6sbJRCrHCqQ1oNRuPpiDvdKbm3NbEE7UXP33fmOVHxEi1NZigOq1EHiQ5_S-41nyyUNd18P0Hn8zKJ4wwesgKMGO7vjJud5hJQygMweIDoX48M2xk-BVLaEHh2ow3cPt3l7JyQ0HNvyzcTatHOD7R_pAlrIU3qlZYJamLDxJpuOOa0yr5W5kHxzwyQxfX3bdWyUkS9XTF7K4VPXwjqgKW4djgv6qw4aLWH-e6Ppg%3D%3D)
We're coming out of the most expensive election in American history. I mean that. Kamala Harris spent over a billion dollars against us. It took EVERY PENNY we had to get our story out there, expose her ultra-Liberal record, reach undecided voters, and win.
So now we're forced to rebuild.
The Democrat Machine is ALREADY crushing us in fundraising, ALREADY outspending us in key races, and ALREADY building the campaign infrastructure to decimate us in the Midterm Elections.
At this point, the consequences of simply resting on our laurels would be unthinkable.
So here's my final pitch to you:
[I’m teaming up with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to raise a million dollars by the end of the month.](http://links.maga-conservatives.com/u/click?_t=da215d85003f407c964bf56cae76557f&_m=a3c55197f3ea4c9787290474c91648a2&_e=yM-Qizn4TtmJyNLJQczr4grhvBRBjr3Ab1pCmK40nYDdpqKPppOuvsEkutKtreJhn0AqQd6Od9gBhc0Qw2UC7CEWdsit0oLv1dfst0waPiIIEu82DfSseZ27qHn1HX_pqIG9vbB0cN7b-sO4pRUSPpDt6TdJ_LKCY0ZozixyNmzXfuBMjdqGK6PqAfK3ZPBj1WZNAkBlgEZa3Udcvua5N4Q_sdihKFh4BZx7x26Qba6wcXmKCCSZDHoXwvj8MEefZ6xplN_Q7Lp0c35DthAp5JFeV5_aFOvWKBfUvCP85W2uGwLVwtVVUwztr35xi-5EQhiJIwYxiyazCfH_pVRq55m8efQzNABkHpChHVdHhWY1yHredaPVkhuuujL8temlxhNqU9wo3aIsH-FZ1X9Ia5t6GAiXRXnKvgVC5idTpncVTXCHCizyf-CuKlpxwi_henTQ_MQQbLLyqu_C2DoxaM2BDtUFwyA3kDnfZKAW6wRQKNwOLSHCaT8kmTCwIKdKiny7egVvUQ9UNsV0EvMgAvpBaRLp20ilqsPtHHMnyVPMM3d3MDhIiIQLU41v_WqlMu10CrqoYaOibRK1-huaqlIzrQx2qAKmoGXsnYHyW1Mil78h9-jg7S2Cgo4xFLeG7GhDXSpX6KZX0wgUmC1LEbE3rYPAnOxRNlZNUEEDS7ZddWWordKlnKpBqrka57RDxVH2Hy9ZUmLi6WIsV9ycuw%3D%3D) I understand that's ambitious. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: One Ray of Sunshine in a Dismal Legislative Session
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/msmomentum-12852636?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
**What a dismal legislative session it’s been so far.**

School choice? Killed by Senate leadership without even a proper debate. The ballot initiative reform? Same story. And if that weren't enough, Governor Reeves just had to veto a bill that was sent to him since it apparently had improper revisions tacked on.

Some of our lawmakers, it turns out, struggle with the process of making law.

**But there’s one ray of sunshine from this session: Mississippi is chipping away at the red tape that has been strangling our healthcare economy.**

For decades, Mississippi has required hospitals and healthcare providers to get government permission - a "Certificate of Need," or CON - before they can open new facilities, add beds, or even buy equipment above a certain price. The aim was to keep healthcare costs down, but it didn't work.

Congress itself scrapped the federal program within a decade. Fifteen other states have abolished their CON laws entirely. But ours has remained and is one of the most restrictive in the country.

In practice, CON laws allow existing providers to block competitors. Less competition means higher prices and fewer choices for patients. It's a racket dressed up as regulation, and MCPP has been part of a coalition fighting to repeal it.

**Two bills - HB3 and HB1622 - passed this session, and they matter.**

HB3 raises the spending thresholds that trigger CON review, in some cases doubling them. That means providers can now upgrade equipment and improve facilities without first asking the state's permission. It directs the Department of Health to study exempting small hospitals from CON rules for dialysis and psychiatric services.

HB1622 arguably goes further. It creates a pilot programme giving small and rural hospitals real CON exemptions - no state approval needed - for a range of services on their campuses and nearby. Hospitals in the Delta, one of the most medically underserved regions in the entire country, get up to two exemptions each.

**Good news for kidney dialysis treatment. HB 1622 specifically allows up to eight new dialysis facilities to be licensed at small rural hospitals, with those decisions final and unchallengeable, which is huge news for the Delta.**

But the single most exciting thing in HB1622 is a simple rule change: if a competitor files an appeal to block a CON approval and loses, they now have to pay the winner's legal costs. That might not sound dramatic, but it's a big deal. For years, this served as a deterrent against challenges.

We are a long way from the full repeal of CON that is required, but these two bills show that the legislative strategy to achieve repeal is viable and it is working.

**If you want to read a recent research paper we published on the implications of these two new laws, please click on the link below:**
---
| [ ](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=1347bab4d7&e=5703353baa)
---

| The dam hasn't broken yet. But it has cracked.

Thank you for your continued support. We'll keep pushing.

**MICHIGAN IS 44TH IN EDUCATION.** Friend, That's embarrassing. That's unacceptable. That's changing. My mission as Governor: Make Michigan the #1 state in the nation for education by 2037 - our state’s 200th birthday. Not 10th. Not 5th. NUMBER ONE. _**Here's the plan:**_
---
