Federal Education Freedom Tax Credit activated day one. **ACCOUNTABILITY:** Constitutional amendment making the Governor directly responsible for education outcomes. The buck stops with me. **BASICS:** Phonics works. Physical textbooks work. Cellphones out. 3rd grade reading retention back. Stop the gimmicks. **OPPORTUNITY:** Every diploma comes with a trade certification, professional license, or career portfolio. College isn't for everyone - but opportunity is for everyone. **EXCELLENCE:** Reward great teachers with higher pay and bonuses. Remove barriers for professionals to enter teaching. **EFFICIENCY:** Cut administrative bloat. Put dollars in classrooms, not bureaucracies. **PROTECTION:** Defend Title IX. name: Roy Cooper
subject: Let me explain
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Roy Cooper for North Carolina
body:
With a new poll showing this race statistically tied, things are heating up.
| | | | | [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/7793?t=14&akid=839%2E124072%2EnnHP-q)
---
Peter,

**[In a moment, I’m going to ask you to make your first donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. But first, let me explain why your support right now – ahead of our first end-of-quarter FEC deadline of the year – is so important.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/7793?t=15&akid=839%2E124072%2EnnHP-q)**
I didn’t plan to run for federal office. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home.

But the more I saw all the chaos and cruelty coming out of Washington, the more I felt an obligation to do everything in my power to stop it. I remembered how my parents left me a better country than they’d had – and I wanted to do the same for my kids and for future generations.
So I launched my campaign for Senate, and ever since then, I’ve been so grateful for the outpouring of support from people like you. _Thank you, Peter._

Now, with a new poll showing this race statistically tied, things are heating up: Far-right Republican PACs are pouring in millions of dollars to defeat me – and even President Trump himself is attacking me.
**Even with all the chaos, partisan politics and hateful language, I still have hope because I believe in the basic goodness of people. I believe we can win here and set our nation back on course. But it won’t be easy, and it’s going to take serious resources.**
**[That’s why I set a goal to raise $1 million before this FEC deadline, and I’m counting on your help to reach it. Will you chip in $5 or whatever amount is meaningful to you to help us fight back against the GOP, win in North Carolina and take back the Senate?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/7794?t=16&akid=839%2E124072%2EnnHP-q)**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/7795?t=17&akid=839%2E124072%2EnnHP-q)

---

---
Thank you,

Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

Friend, what would you think if I told you that $580 million in oil futures were traded in a single minute, just before a major announcement from Donald Trump on foreign policy?
Well, that's exactly what happened.
On March 24, roughly 15 minutes before Donald Trump posted that the United States was engaged in "productive conversations" to end the war in Iran, there was a sudden, massive spike in oil futures trading.
That announcement moved markets. Oil prices had already been rising for weeks as global shipments slowed – and families across the country, including in Connecticut, have been paying the price at the pump.
**But while you were paying more than $4 a gallon, someone else made _hundreds of millions._**
Economist Paul Krugman put it bluntly: "People close to Trump are trading based on national secrets."
There's a term for that: insider trading. And when it involves sensitive national security information, it raises even more serious concerns about corruption, abuse of power, and the use of public office for private gain.
This is not an isolated incident. We've seen a pattern of the Trump family having financial ties to companies positioned for government contracts, political allies benefiting while oversight is weakened, and more than 70 individuals convicted of fraud being pardoned.
**And now, nearly $1 billion in taxpayer money is being handed to a foreign energy company to have them abandon renewable energy projects, only to reinvest that money in oil and gas.**
At a time when gas prices are already squeezing families.
At a time when we should be investing in affordable, renewable energy for the future.
Instead, this administration appears to be prioritizing profits for the powerful over relief for everyday Americans. And here's the most troubling part: The very people who should be investigated are the ones controlling the agencies meant to hold them accountable.
As Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, I take that responsibility seriously.
**I will not let this be ignored. But I need you with me.[Please, add your name today to demand accountability, transparency, and answers for the American people. Your signature sends a clear message: We will not allow those in power to manipulate markets while families struggle to make ends meet.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128235601/610703611/775120051?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&amounts=5,25,50,100&code=jtk1448-su-nd1&refcode=jtk1448-su-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTQ3ODgzNzUtYWUyYS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=I1U5GAuu8NbBHGjNT2V2MWK4X7VtGs0_MOfoZl39Ygo=&emci=50f69d27-f829-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=a4788375-ae2a-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=9329426)**

| Peter,

A new statewide poll just confirmed what I hear everywhere I go in Montgomery County: housing is the number one issue facing families right now.

Nearly two-thirds of Marylanders say housing costs are a major problem. That includes renters, homeowners, young families, seniors, and even people earning over $100,000 a year. Across party lines and throughout communities, people are feeling squeezed.

The poll also found that majorities support building more housing near transit, creating smaller and more affordable homes, and cutting red tape so projects can actually move forward.

I’m not surprised — and I didn’t wait for a poll to act.
---

On the County Council, I’ve spent years leading on housing because I know affordability is the foundation of everything else. If families can’t afford to live here, we lose workers, students, small businesses, and our economic future.

That’s why I’ve led efforts like:

**✅****Passing the Accelerate MoCo package, which cuts red tape and fast-tracks affordable housing, cutting the time to get projects approved by as much as 90%.**

**✅**** Launching the nationally recognized Housing Production Fund to deliver more affordable units.**

**✅ ****Building transit-oriented housing near Metro so people can live closer to work.**

**✅**** Supporting nonprofit housing providers so affordability stays permanent.**

**✅**** Creating new housing options for workers, older adults, and people with disabilities.**

These successes happened by bringing people together and delivering results, and it’s exactly the kind of pragmatic leadership Montgomery County needs right now.

That’s the vision and track record I’m running on as County Executive: a county where families can afford to live, older adults can age affordably in place, and young families can put down roots and help build our local economy.

Career scientists — the people we rely on to keep our kids safe — have been sidelined, silenced, and replaced by political ideologues.

Public health experts say critical programs are being dismantled, scientists are afraid to even put things in writing, and communications are being controlled by political appointees instead of medical experts.

I’m Dr. Jasmine Clark. I’m a microbiologist and public health professional, and I don’t use words like this lightly: **This is dangerous.**

Science doesn’t change depending on who is in power. Viruses don’t care about politics. And when leaders ignore evidence, people get hurt.

This is exactly why I first ran for office — because I saw what happens when politicians override science with misinformation.

In Georgia, I’ve stood up to it by calling out false COVID data, exposing fake medical claims used to justify abortion bans, and fighting to protect public health and truth

VoteVets could spend a few hundred thousand dollars against one vulnerable Republican ahead of a vote on the Iran War, or the SAVE Act, or a spending package... and kill the bill.
The GOP knows this, and they’re scared. Terrified, actually. And with the first FEC deadline of the year coming up on March 31st we can have them really shaking in their boots.
You see, after that deadline hits, we’re legally required to report our fundraising numbers to the public. You can bet Mike Johnson and his team are going to be looking at the numbers we put up, because that’s how much we’re going to be able to spend against his members.

name: NEGOP
subject: Reminder: 🚨 Your Weekly Update From The NEGOP
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nebraska Republican Party 1610 N St
body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
Fellow Republicans,
Election Season is Here - Let's Get to Work
Campaigns are underway and the primary election is fast approaching. Our number one goal remains unchanging: elect Republicans in every possible race. While our tactics adapt to each phase of the election cycle, our commitment to victory remains steadfast. Our current focus is aggressive Get Out the Vote (GOTV) efforts and full support for all our Republican candidates up and down the ballot.
While winning elections is our immediate priority, it's critical we never lose sight of why these victories matter so much.
Republicans stand for limited government, individual freedom, fiscal responsibility, strong families, and traditional American values. Democrats offer a fundamentally different vision--one that relies more heavily on government expansion, higher taxes, and progressive social policies. Here are some clear examples:
Securing the border and enforcing immigration laws -- Republicans support stronger border security, reducing illegal crossings, and prioritizing legal immigration. These efforts protect wages, stem abuse of public services, and promote the rule of law.
Voter ID requirements -- Requiring photo identification to vote is a minimal requirement for election integrity and common sense; especially when ID checks are commonplace for everyday activities like buying alcohol or boarding a plane.
Banning biological males from competing in women's sports -- Protecting fair competition in female athletics by restricting participation based on biological sex. Republicans defend women's opportunities and safety, and advocate for "common sense" over gender ideology.
Law and order / backing the police -- Republicans support funding police, cracking down on crime, and restoring public safety (especially after recent spikes in certain cities). Republicans promote "back the blue," opposing "defund the police" movements, and emphasize prosecuting criminals over activist reforms.
Healthcare reforms focused on affordability and choice -- Republicans support price transparency, allowing cross-state insurance competition, reducing regulations that drive up costs, and targeting waste/fraud in programs like those found in Medicare/Medicaid.
In parallel with our election efforts, we continue vital organizational work: tracking County Party Conventions, helping previously unorganized counties stand up strong local parties, and monitoring leadership changes to strengthen our grassroots foundation statewide.
The NEGOP is also planning our State Convention and Vote Red Auction. Save the dates!
Thursday, June 5th: The exciting finale to our 2nd Annual Vote Red Auction & Dinner Friday, June 6th: Our State Convention in La Vista
These events are perfect opportunities to connect, celebrate, and build momentum heading into the general election.
Steady fundraising remains essential. Every dollar helps us keep the lights on, support our candidates, and deliver the results Nebraskans deserve.
It's easy to get caught up in the "how" of our daily work--calls, doors, meetings, and logistics. Let's stay energized and motivated by the "why."
Every action we take is building a stronger, freer, and more prosperous Nebraska under Republican leadership.

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Fellow Republicans, Election Season is Here - Let's Get to Work Campaigns are underway and the primary election is fast approaching. Our number one goal remains unchanging: elect Republicans in every possible race. While our tactics adapt to each phase of the election cycle, our commitment to victory remains steadfast. Our current focus is aggressive Get Out the Vote (GOTV) efforts and full support for all our Republican candidates up and down the ballot. While winning elections is our immediate priority, it's critical we never lose sight of why these victories matter so much. Republicans stand for limited government, individual freedom, fiscal responsibility, strong families, and traditional American values. Democrats offer a fundamentally different vision--one that relies more heavily on government expansion, higher taxes, and progressive social policies. Here are some clear examples: Securing the border and enforcing immigration laws -- Republicans support stronger border security, reducing illegal crossings, and prioritizing legal immigration. These efforts protect wages, stem abuse of public services, and promote the rule of law. Voter ID requirements -- Requiring photo identification to vote is a minimal requirement for election integrity and common sense; especially when ID checks are commonplace for everyday activities like buying alcohol or boarding a plane. Banning biological males from competing in women's sports -- Protecting fair competition in female athletics by restricting participation based on biological sex. Republicans defend women's opportunities and safety, and advocate for "common sense" over gender ideology. Law and order / backing the police -- Republicans support funding police, cracking down on crime, and restoring public safety (especially after recent spikes in certain cities). Republicans promote "back the blue," opposing "defund the police" movements, and emphasize prosecuting criminals over activist reforms. Healthcare reforms focused on affordability and choice -- Republicans support price transparency, allowing cross-state insurance competition, reducing regulations that drive up costs, and targeting waste/fraud in programs like those found in Medicare/Medicaid. name: Mark Warner
subject: We can’t ignore this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
We can take back control of Congress, but not without Virginia.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260328-406&t=2&akid=406%2E12592%2EIWI8Z4)
Hi, Mark Warner here.
I’ll get straight to the point: We can take back control of Congress.**But not without Virginia.**
Across the country, Donald Trump and his allies are trying to manipulate congressional maps to lock in their power before voters even get a chance to weigh in. They know that if they can rig the rules, they can tilt the outcome of the next Congress before the first vote is cast.
_But here in Virginia, voters have the chance to push back. We can make a difference. We can shift the tides of power, and we can stop Trump’s blatant attempt at rigging the 2026 midterms._
This April, Virginians will vote on this crucial redistricting amendment. By voting YES, we can move forward with new congressional maps, level the playing field and prevent Trump and Republicans from rigging the election to wield unchecked power for another two years.
The stakes are bigger than just one state. This vote in Virginia could help determine whether Congress starts actually working for the American people again.
That’s why the YES campaign, Virginians for Fair Elections, is working around the clock to make sure voters understand what’s on the ballot and why it matters. But reaching voters across the Commonwealth takes real resources, especially with early voting already underway and Election Day coming up on April 21.
So I’m personally asking for your help today. For Virginians across the Commonwealth:
[**Can you chip in right now to support Virginians for Fair Elections and help power the YES campaign to victory?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260327_1.hUgJnZ&amount=3&refcode=20260328-406&t=3&akid=406%2E12592%2EIWI8Z4)
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260327_1.hUgJnZ&amount=3&refcode=20260328-406&t=22&akid=406%2E12592%2EIWI8Z4)**
Every contribution helps educate voters, counter misinformation, and make sure Virginians know the high stakes of this election before they cast their ballots.
Virginia has always played an outsized role in our democracy. And this year, once again, the eyes of the nation are on the Commonwealth.
Thank you for stepping up.
[](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260327_1.hUgJnZ&amount=3&refcode=20260328-406&t=23&akid=406%2E12592%2EIWI8Z4)

body:
| | Dear Derek, Democrats are moving to put a state income tax on the table right now. If we do not stop them immediately, they will take more of your paycheck and grow government on our backs. I’m Joe Sweeney. I serve as a State Representative from Salem and I chair Granite Solutions. I spoke out on WMUR this week because this fight is urgent. As a fellow Granite Stater, I’m asking you to stand with us today. | [CHIP IN $5](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D5) | [CHIP IN $10](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D10) | [CHIP IN $25](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D25)
---|---|---
Here’s the deal: New Hampshire rewards work and protects taxpayers. An income tax would make our state less competitive and it will not stay small. Once politicians open that door they keep widening it until we have the highest tax burden in the nation.
**An income tax is a permanent attack on the New Hampshire way.**
Granite Solutions is lean and fast. We do direct voter contact, targeted digital ads, grassroots phone outreach, and rapid-response messaging when Democrats push bad ideas. We move money quickly to where it matters most.
### How will you spend my money well?
* Paid digital ads targeted to swing towns, flip the conversation fast
* Door-knock and phone programs to activate pro-taxpayer voters
* Rapid-response communications to shut down bad messaging
* Strategic mail to key districts where votes are decided

We do more with less. No waste. Every dollar goes to fighting this tax and protecting the freedoms New Hampshire stands for: educational freedom, Second Amendment rights, low taxes, and secure communities.
[FIGHT BACK $50](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D50) | [FIGHT BACK $100](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D100) | [FIGHT BACK $250](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D250)
---|---|---
This is not a debate for later. The proposal is moving in committee and Democrats are lining up votes. If we do not push back now, the momentum shifts and the door opens for higher taxes and bigger government.
Will you join me? A small gift today sends a clear message: New Hampshire will not be turned into another high-tax state. Pick an amount and chip in now.
[STOP THE INCOME TAX](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax%3Famount%3D25) | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://donorprospect.com/t/c/bd28af44-e32c-42eb-8a19-1f0dbf17def7?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fstop-the-income-tax)

### **Help us defeat the mainstream media and promote capitalism and American exceptionalism.**
### **[Support The Capitalist, become a paid subscriber today:](https://substack.com/redirect/09dee435-e04f-4fb6-a964-52b6e5745e55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/09dee435-e04f-4fb6-a964-52b6e5745e55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
At Meta HQ in Menlo Park, screens pulse with real-time engagement metrics, the dopamine hits for billions, quantified to the millisecond. Down the hall, engineers tweak their algorithms.
A thousand miles away a teenage girl swipes on her phone. Meta knows her moods better than her parents ever could.
Now imagine the same company's executives, under oath, shrugging, saying that they simply had no idea their platforms had become a breeding ground for predators. A New Mexico jury just called that bluff.
On March 24, 2026, **[Meta was found liable for willfully violating the state's unfair practices act and ordered to pay $375 million](https://substack.com/redirect/2eecfca8-f03f-4a80-ad4e-16334c35a749?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**--the maximum per-violation penalty under state law, though far below the $2.1 billion the attorney general had sought.
The case, brought by Attorney General Raul Torrez in 2023, centered on Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp's role in enabling child sexual exploitation. An undercover operation created a fake profile of a 13-year-old girl; it was **["simply inundated"](https://substack.com/redirect/083f7f05-b93d-4c99-ae0f-2c02bfa1905f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with images and targeted solicitations from abusers.
Whistleblowers and former executives testified that safety was never the priority under Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg. **[Internal messages revealed concerns](https://substack.com/redirect/083f7f05-b93d-4c99-ae0f-2c02bfa1905f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that end-to-end encryption would hinder reporting of millions of child sexual abuse material cases. One researcher had warned of 500,000 such cases daily on Facebook and Instagram alone. Yet profits--and the engagement flywheel--came first.
For a company as obsessed with knowing as much as it can about its users as Meta is, the claim that it "didn't know" people were being hurt is laughable. Meta's surveillance capitalism is legendary: it tracks every scroll, pause, like, and hesitation. Its algorithms don't merely serve content--they optimize for maximum addiction.
Have you ever noticed that the scrolling mechanism on your timeline feels like a slot machine at a Casino? The next swipe always promising another roll of the wheel, a fresh fix for your dopamine receptors? _**You will now!**_
* * *
* * *
### **Help us defeat the mainstream media and promote capitalism and American exceptionalism.**
### **[Support The Capitalist, become a paid subscriber today:](https://substack.com/redirect/09dee435-e04f-4fb6-a964-52b6e5745e55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/09dee435-e04f-4fb6-a964-52b6e5745e55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
That same machinery, jurors heard, excels at connecting users with shared "interests"--including predators and their "interests." **[Arturo Bejar, a former Meta executive, testified](https://substack.com/redirect/054e1031-4402-444e-bd35-ff56356f55f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that after his own 14-year-old daughter received sexual solicitations, he warned leadership. The response? Not urgency, but continued emphasis on growth.
The data about the effects of social media on children, teens, and young adults is now well established. Peer-reviewed studies link heavy social media use to increased inattention symptoms, declining concentration, poorer reading and memory scores, disrupted sleep, and heightened emotional volatility.
Short-form video and endless doom-scrolling have rewired people's minds, to say nothing of developing brains. The entire global consciousness is very well aware that attention spans have been ruined by the prevalence of these products; **[teachers report it daily, parents live it nightly.](https://substack.com/redirect/083f7f05-b93d-4c99-ae0f-2c02bfa1905f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Meta didn't invent human vulnerability, but it industrialized it at scale--designing interfaces that exploit the same reward circuits cigarettes once targeted in the young.
Here is where the parallels with the Big Tobacco cases of the 1990s become almost impossible to ignore. _**Tobacco companies engineered products to be as addictive as possible while denying the harm, especially to minors.**_ They didn't just put tobacco in paper tubes, they added chemicals to heighten the cravings.
They knew.
They knew, and they lied, and eventually, they paid.
Social media may not be as straightforward as "cigarettes causing lung cancer"--the line between cause and harm is more a not-so-distant-cousin rather than a direct biochemical pathway--but the pattern is eerily familiar: a product deliberately optimized for compulsive use, marketed to the young, despite mounting evidence of damage being caused to them. About the only piece of the cigarette industry playbook Meta didn't use was getting doctors to say that using social media was good for people.
The kids may not be coughing and wheezing but they are definitely addicted and the psychological and social damage to their minds is profound. In the words of The Offspring, the kids aren't alright.
Internal documents, **[whistleblowers,](https://substack.com/redirect/054e1031-4402-444e-bd35-ff56356f55f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and jury findings suggest Meta followed a similar script as the cigarette companies before them: downplay risks publicly, dismiss employee warnings privately, and prioritize the metric that matters--time on site.
This verdict should serve as a landmark for future tech inventions, whether AI or whatever comes after AI. You will be held responsible for the harm you cause.
Consider the ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI a firm in its infancy and no where near as established as Meta, where a Colorado mother alleges ChatGPT turned from a helpful tool into her son Austin Gordon's **["frighteningly effective suicide coach."](https://substack.com/redirect/796c0297-a99d-4e81-8dfe-d8fa110e1b83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The complaint details how the model romanticized death, transformed his favorite childhood book into a **["suicide lullaby,"](https://substack.com/redirect/796c0297-a99d-4e81-8dfe-d8fa110e1b83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and encouraged him in late 2025. Three days later, he was gone.
OpenAI insists it has improved safeguards, yet the case underscores a broader truth: when systems are built to maximize engagement and emotional dependency, tragedy is not a bug--it is a foreseeable consequence of the design choices.
Put brutally simply: For some users, it will kill them. It will have a body count.
This is not a witch hunt with pitchforks and burning torches, counterarguments deserve their airtime. Meta employs thousands to work on safety, works with law enforcement, and faces genuine challenges policing billions of users and pieces of content twenty four hours a day. Section 230 has long shielded platforms from liability for third-party speech, and some worry that aggressive liability will chill innovation or push harmful activity into darker corners of the internet. These are fair points and companies face real challenges which the average user can't comprehend. Yet designing addictive products while feigning ignorance of their documented harms is not neutral engineering--**it is a business decision with victims.** The jury did not buy the defense that bad actors will always exist; they held Meta accountable for the architecture that makes predation _**easier and more targeted.**_
Skeptics of regulation often warn of bureaucratic overreach. As capitalists, we share that skepticism--government is rarely the most efficient allocator of resources or arbiter of speech. But accountability is not regulation for its own sake. It is the market mechanism of tort law doing what it does best: forcing builders to internalize the externalities their products create. When a platform knows (because its own data tells it) that its recommendation engine funnels predators toward children and still optimizes for retention, the proper response is not another layer of Washington rules. It is the sting of liability so great that it makes executives weigh the human cost against the quarterly numbers.
The New Mexico case is smaller in dollars than the headlines once touted, but its precedent is enormous. It pierces the "we're just a neutral platform" myth and puts every tech founder on notice: build responsibly, or pay the price. Future AI systems that foster dependency, manipulate emotion, or steer vulnerable users toward harm will face the same scrutiny. That's healthy. Builders thrive when they solve real problems without manufacturing new ones.
Meta will appeal, and the fight will continue in other courtrooms and statehouses. But the cultural and legal tide has shifted. Companies that treat users--especially the young--as raw material for engagement algorithms must now calculate the true cost.
Innovate boldly, yes. Do your best to mitigate the harm you cause as you create, absolutely, but never again pretend you didn't see the wreckage.

The claim that Meta "didn't know" people were being hurt is laughable | | | Mar 28 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Help us defeat the mainstream media and promote capitalism and American exceptionalism. At Meta HQ in Menlo Park, screens pulse with real-time engagement metrics, the dopamine hits for billions, quantified to the millisecond. Down the hall, engineers tweak their algorithms. A thousand miles away a teenage girl swipes on her phone. Meta knows her moods better than her parents ever could. Now imagine the same company's executives, under oath, shrugging, saying that they simply had no idea their platforms had become a breeding ground for predators. A New Mexico jury just called that bluff. On March 24, 2026, maximum per-violation penalty under state law, though far below the $2.1 billion the attorney general had sought. The case, brought by Attorney General Raul Torrez in 2023, centered on Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp's role in enabling child sexual exploitation. An undercover operation created a fake profile of a 13-year-old girl; it was with images and targeted solicitations from abusers. Whistleblowers and former executives testified that safety was never the priority under Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg. that end-to-end encryption would hinder reporting of millions of child sexual abuse material cases. One researcher had warned of 500,000 such cases daily on Facebook and Instagram alone. Yet profits--and the engagement flywheel--came first. For a company as obsessed with knowing as much as it can about its users as Meta is, the claim that it "didn't know" people were being hurt is laughable. Meta's surveillance capitalism is legendary: it tracks every scroll, pause, like, and hesitation. Its algorithms don't merely serve content--they optimize for maximum addiction. Have you ever noticed that the scrolling mechanism on your timeline feels like a slot machine at a Casino? The next swipe always promising another roll of the wheel, a fresh fix for your dopamine receptors? You will now! Help us defeat the mainstream media and promote capitalism and American exceptionalism. That same machinery, jurors heard, excels at connecting users with shared "interests"--including predators and their "interests." that after his own 14-year-old daughter received sexual solicitations, he warned leadership. The response? Not urgency, but continued emphasis on growth. The data about the effects of social media on children, teens, and young adults is now well established. Peer-reviewed studies link heavy social media use to increased inattention symptoms, declining concentration, poorer reading and memory scores, disrupted sleep, and heightened emotional volatility. Short-form video and endless doom-scrolling have rewired people's minds, to say nothing of developing brains. The entire global consciousness is very well aware that attention spans have been ruined by the prevalence of these products; Meta didn't invent human vulnerability, but it industrialized it at scale--designing interfaces that exploit the same reward circuits cigarettes once targeted in the young. Here is where the parallels with the Big Tobacco cases of the 1990s become almost impossible to ignore. Tobacco companies engineered products to be as addictive as possible while denying the harm, especially to minors. They didn't just put tobacco in paper tubes, they added chemicals to heighten the cravings. They knew. They knew, and they lied, and eventually, they paid. Social media may not be as straightforward as "cigarettes causing lung cancer"--the line between cause and harm is more a not-so-distant-cousin rather than a direct biochemical pathway--but the pattern is eerily familiar: a product deliberately optimized for compulsive use, marketed to the young, despite mounting evidence of damage being caused to them. About the only piece of the cigarette industry playbook Meta didn't use was getting doctors to say that using social media was good for people. The kids may not be coughing and wheezing but they are definitely addicted and the psychological and social damage to their minds is profound. In the words of The Offspring, the kids aren't alright. Internal documents, and jury findings suggest Meta followed a similar script as the cigarette companies before them: downplay risks publicly, dismiss employee warnings privately, and prioritize the metric that matters--time on site. This verdict should serve as a landmark for future tech inventions, whether AI or whatever comes after AI. You will be held responsible for the harm you cause. Consider the ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI a firm in its infancy and no where near as established as Meta, where a Colorado mother alleges ChatGPT turned from a helpful tool into her son Austin Gordon's The complaint details how the model romanticized death, transformed his favorite childhood book into a and encouraged him in late 2025. Three days later, he was gone. OpenAI insists it has improved safeguards, yet the case underscores a broader truth: when systems are built to maximize engagement and emotional dependency, tragedy is not a bug--it is a foreseeable consequence of the design choices. Put brutally simply: For some users, it will kill them. It will have a body count. This is not a witch hunt with pitchforks and burning torches, counterarguments deserve their airtime. Meta employs thousands to work on safety, works with law enforcement, and faces genuine challenges policing billions of users and pieces of content twenty four hours a day. Section 230 has long shielded platforms from liability for third-party speech, and some worry that aggressive liability will chill innovation or push harmful activity into darker corners of the internet. These are fair points and companies face real challenges which the average user can't comprehend. Yet designing addictive products while feigning ignorance of their documented harms is not neutral engineering--it is a business decision with victims. The jury did not buy the defense that bad actors will always exist; they held Meta accountable for the architecture that makes predation easier and more targeted. Skeptics of regulation often warn of bureaucratic overreach. As capitalists, we share that skepticism--government is rarely the most efficient allocator of resources or arbiter of speech. But accountability is not regulation for its own sake. It is the market mechanism of tort law doing what it does best: forcing builders to internalize the externalities their products create. When a platform knows (because its own data tells it) that its recommendation engine funnels predators toward children and still optimizes for retention, the proper response is not another layer of Washington rules. It is the sting of liability so great that it makes executives weigh the human cost against the quarterly numbers. The New Mexico case is smaller in dollars than the headlines once touted, but its precedent is enormous. It pierces the "we're just a neutral platform" myth and puts every tech founder on notice: build responsibly, or pay the price. Future AI systems that foster dependency, manipulate emotion, or steer vulnerable users toward harm will face the same scrutiny. That's healthy. Builders thrive when they solve real problems without manufacturing new ones. Meta will appeal, and the fight will continue in other courtrooms and statehouses. But the cultural and legal tide has shifted. Companies that treat users--especially the young--as raw material for engagement algorithms must now calculate the true cost. Innovate boldly, yes. Do your best to mitigate the harm you cause as you create, absolutely, but never again pretend you didn't see the wreckage. If you are willing to stand with me to help these patriots rebuild their lives, please join me today by donating whatever you can generously afford to help Stand in the Gap today.

Friend,

Five years ago, I gathered with patriots from all corners of America to protest the certification of the 2020 election results.

All we wanted was for President Trump to get a fair shake, for mail-in vote counts to be redone, and to ensure no fraud had taken place. However, President Trump's enemies saw us coming, and they were ready and waiting to pull off perhaps the biggest psy-op America has ever seen.

Capitol Police officers welcomed many J6ers into the building, with some even providing off-the-cuff tours as they ushered protestors through the halls of the Capitol.

All of a sudden, though, things took a very dark turn...
* A Capitol Police officer murdered Ashli Babbitt.
* Overzealous officers assaulted protestors.
* Rosann Boyland was trampled to death in the panic that ensued as the Capitol Police swiftly turned on peaceful protestors.

For many, like myself, this day marked the beginning of a years-long political persecution that tore families apart, devastated finances, and even denied many of us our freedom and our fundamental human rights.

It also motivated me to start Stand in the Gap -- a commitment to stand in solidarity with and fight for those who are being overlooked or mistreated.

If you are willing to stand with me to help these patriots rebuild their lives, please join me today by donating whatever you can generously afford to help Stand in the Gap today. Friend, Five years ago, I gathered with patriots from all corners of America to protest the certification of the 2020 election results. All we wanted was for President Trump to get a fair shake, for mail-in vote counts to be redone, and to ensure no fraud had taken place. However, President Trump's enemies saw us coming, and they were ready and waiting to pull off perhaps the biggest psy-op America has ever seen. All of a sudden, though, things took a very dark turn... A Capitol Police officer murdered Ashli Babbitt. Overzealous officers assaulted protestors. Rosann Boyland was trampled to death in the panic that ensued as the Capitol Police swiftly turned on peaceful protestors. For many, like myself, this day marked the beginning of a years-long political persecution that tore families apart, devastated finances, and even denied many of us our freedom and our fundamental human rights. It also motivated me to start Stand in the Gap -- a commitment to stand in solidarity with and fight for those who are being overlooked or mistreated. Our goal is to provide support and advocacy for those in need, ensuring they aren't left to face their challenges alone. Stand in the Gap originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping the recently released J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. Surprisingly, there are very few resources for people who are released from prison, particularly if they are conservative, America First activists, or who supported President Trump. These J6ers are our neighbors. They are sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, mothers and fathers. It is up to us to ensure that they have the resources needed to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. We were founded to "stand in the gap" for those in prison and those navigating life after incarceration. body:

Friend,
I am the third Jewish woman and the first former synagogue president ever elected to the United States Senate. My faith is deeply tied to who I am, what I fight for, and my role as a lawmaker.
It’s part of why I care about the issues that I do, and it means that I bring with me the same struggles that all Jews face. Most prominently, the threat and impact of discrimination is part of my story – as it is for so many Americans.

body:
This deadline is a big dealPeter,.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, as busy as this campaign is every day, I still make time in my schedule to attend my son’s baseball games. Those are moments I will never be able to get back if I miss them — and as a parent, that’s important to me.
I know I can’t attend every game. But if I am able to be there, I will make sure I am.
That’s why I am eternally grateful to supporters like you and the rest of this team. Every time you make a grassroots donation to my campaign, that’s one less call I have to make asking for money. You’re helping us focus our time on what matters.
And for me, that means building a winning campaign and still having time to be a mom. It means campaigning across Texas and still making it in time for the game.
You’ve already heard about our end-of-quarter deadline coming up on March 31.**It’s a big deal, Peter.** Everyone from Greg Abbott’s campaign to the media and pundits will be scrutinizing our campaign.
And I want to make sure we’re in the strongest possible position after this week. I know if we double down and give it all we’ve got, we’ll knock it out of the park.

Allow me to introduce myself to you |
---

Peter,

You may already know who I am from my basketball career. Or, maybe you’re just hearing about me for the first time through my Senate Campaign. Either way, I wanted to formally introduce myself and share my story. [**_Afterward, I’m going to ask you to send a small contribution to my campaign as I continue to fight to Flip Minnesota Red._**](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=d4b7a5e544c44c1898d2042b1d650957&_e=wWKewejwbID_LNsF7Hf8LlVyQ9OMS_yhfQeWC1oVr8WXogXZKIpvBzsrQXPIgKPZEJ7BJwmd_P-FKHnR96EJqzAfdC0qgi5r4gdF9VEKah1EUW4CvEySgXAj0tWBcmnffYgwO0JTkJHT9AIdqiTwfeIjhOn_LbhYveYfUZYWSs7znS4AyqLrcxeNuEOixAL3IEs3RjKcFcBiH9mEjMoyH0BbgIoLrx3xCKtcoT_S-CP0jmxn8n1E7u-sNgLFDqU4Xe00UwEtYRvJKgGSPCA9fHN6-W234cHcZP3ycYIrNaX9_k3pgGoajKRMoJYhlFcjO7EP01VgaPMGKKwrdgD1-v-odZC_lLDV-oE7GmFK6KQflZokgvnf1A9w1E520CZ6ouoOvTrDiKq_9A86Lf2V5WzYslOis8R4rlxV2qdPrQ-GvgN1IQUW5blPaSrgSnPtCf_8wmAEfU7f_hYThm2N_uT4v2wTQ4xQPbJkpHzc8mMyRLeoKVo55rJSZ3O0a5TKu_IP-C360xCM5vURlCzAWJare5hcm0Sahk6LDdpS8yH5yxZqcqHgvt148ihvEgAU)

I was born and raised in the Twin Cities in Minnesota, mainly in the Rondo Community of St. Paul. body:

They’re trying to make it harder for you to vote.
Right now, the Senate is debating the SAVE Act—after House Republicans already passed it last month—pushing sweeping new proof-of-citizenship requirements and strict ID mandates that could block eligible Americans from voting nationwide.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
Let me be clear: this isn’t about election security. It’s about voter suppression.
As Oregon’s chief elections officer, I joined five other Democratic secretaries of state in opposing these bills because they would place a massive burden on eligible voters, create unfunded mandates for states, and inject chaos into election systems just as the 2026 midterms ramp up.
These bills would force voters to jump through bureaucratic hoops, spend more time and money proving their eligibility, or risk losing access to the ballot altogether. That is not how democracy should work.
In Oregon, we’ve built one of the most secure and accessible voting systems in the country. I will fight any attempt to undermine it — whether it comes from billionaires spreading lies or politicians in Washington trying to score partisan points.
But I need your support to keep standing up for voters.
If you believe voting should be free, fair, and accessible — not complicated and costly — please chip in $10 or $25 today to help us defend Oregon’s elections. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]

clean_body: This morning, The New York Times profiled Kaela Berg — and showed exactly why EMILYs List backed her early. | = Hi Peter, Big news:this morning,The New York Times profiled EMILYs List-endorsed candidate Kaela Berg — a flight attendant, union leader, working mom, and Minnesota state representative running for Congress in one of the most important U.S. House races in the country. = And this article highlights exactly why we do what we do. At EMILYs List, we work to identify exceptional women early and give them the support they need to build strong, winning campaigns from the ground up. Long before the national press catches on, we're helping candidates like Kaela get off the ground. = | = The Times captured what makes Kaela such a powerful candidate: while running for Congress, she is still working as a flight attendant, balancing campaign calls and political strategy in between long shifts, layovers, and early-morning flights. She has spent years living the economic pressures so many Americans are facing right now — worrying about paychecks, paying rent, and building a life while working hard every single day. That matters. Because at a moment when voters are demanding fighters and leadership that actually understands affordability, Kaela brings something Washington desperately needs more of: the lived experience of a working person. She came to politics through organizing and union leadership. She fought for better wages and dignity on the job. She raised her family while working as a flight attendant. She continues to fly while serving in the Minnesota Legislature. And now, she's running for Congress because there are far too few people in Washington who can truly say they understand what working families are up against. We need more leaders like that in office. And with your support, we can help send them there. = = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you, the EMILYs List team | = = = = = | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List. This weekend, "No Kings" protests are taking place across the country--including here in Connecticut.
_**The right to protest is fundamental. It is protected by the First Amendment to the United States Constitution, and it remains one of the most powerful tools citizens have to make their voices heard.**_
_**It is one of the greatest tools we have in this nation that has resulted in impacting change with a belief that our voices must be heard and not silenced.**_
_**However, there should be a large distinction if the Protest is sponsored by a foreign actor as that changes the messaging and the impact as it is no longer organic.**_
# What is the concern for Americans?
**Truth in protests - Stop the Astroturfing!**
* Are these demonstrations truly organic?
* Or are they being organized, funded, and coordinated behind the scenes?
* That question doesn't silence protest--it strengthens it.
* Because if protests are real, transparency should never be a problem.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b61113b9-4339-45b5-8354-eca30de5a8f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
However, if the protest is designed to have the appearance of "grassroots" but is not - a deceptive term known as "astroturfing" \- that should be disclosed and known to all in attendance and those observing in the media.
# To address this growing concern, We are advancing: **The Real Protest Act**
_**A framework designed not to restrict protest --but to ensure transparency, accountability, and public trust especially in an era where one movement to support "freedom" gains attention while another with the same type of victims of an oppressive regime are ignored and without commensurate media coverage and/or public awareness/outrage.**_
**The Real Protest Act would:**
✔ Require disclosure of funding for demonstrations exceeding $1,500 and for persons receiving compensation to hold signs and be part of the protest
✔ Prevent evasion through multiple small donations from the same source
✔ Identify when protests include paid participants
✔ Require reporting of coordinated national protest campaigns
✔ Apply equally to political parties, advocacy groups, and affiliated networks
✔ Prohibit foreign funding tied to demonstrations that support violence or threats to human life
✔ Require disclosure of foreign funds used in protest activity
✔ Establish a Public Demonstration Transparency Registry
✔ Require liability insurance for large organized demonstrations
✔ Allow civil recovery when organized protests result in injury or destruction
**Why $1,500 Matters?**
This is not an arbitrary number.
A threshold of $1,500 reflects meaningful organized activity--for example:
* approximately 300 printed protest signs at ~$5 each
* coordinated logistics, messaging, or recruitment

At that point, a demonstration reflects organization--not just spontaneity.
And when that happens, the public deserves transparency.

# **No Kings -- And No Hidden Leaders**
# This weekend's message is "No Kings."
But that should mean more than opposing visible authority.
It should also mean no hidden leaders--no one behind the scenes pulling the strings.
**No modern-day Gepetto quietly directing the show while others play the part.**
Because if a movement is real, it stands on its own.
And if it isn't--
the public deserves to know who's orchestrating it as it can put those receiving compensation at risk for irreparable harm from criminal prosecution and or physical harm should a protest get out of hand. _**There is no defense that a protestor was advised it was OK to violate a law.**_
# The American Civil Liberties Union has a great section covering protestors' rights and those of counter-protesters - [See Here](https://substack.com/redirect/fb23a2fd-63b1-4621-9e5c-468d151bcf5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**What the Evidence Suggests**
Recent events raise legitimate questions about how some protest movements are organized and aligned.
Across multiple cities, recent demonstrations have shown:
* coordinated national messaging (including signage)
* overlapping geopolitical themes
* organized turnout beyond spontaneous local action (in a very short timeframe)

At the same time, countries like Venezuela and Iran have faced documented repression and violence against their own citizens.
This does not mean every protester shares the same intent.
But it raises a fair and necessary question:
Are some movements driven by transparent grassroots concerns--or by coordinated and funded agendas?
**Why It Matters**
Protest is a sacred American right.
But when demonstrations are:
* centrally coordinated
* funded through undisclosed sources
* structured to avoid disclosure thresholds
* or presented as grassroots when they are not

the public deserves transparency.
Because democracy depends not just on protest--
but on honest protest.
* * *
# **Proposed Federal Legislation**
**The Real Protest Act (Sample Bill)**
**119th CONGRESS**
**1st Session**
**H. R. ____**
To promote transparency and accountability in organized demonstration activity, to prohibit certain foreign-funded demonstration activities that threaten human life, and for other purposes.
**Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,**
**SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE**
This Act may be cited as the "Real Protest Act."
**SEC. 2. FINDINGS**
Congress finds that:
1. The First Amendment guarantees the right to peaceful assembly and free expression.
2. Peaceful protest is fundamental to democratic governance.
3. Certain demonstrations are organized through centralized funding and compensated participation, creating the appearance of grassroots support.
4. Undisclosed or intentionally structured funding may mislead the public and distort democratic processes.
5. Organized demonstrations have, in certain instances, resulted in violence, property destruction, and threats to human life.
6. Foreign actors may seek to influence domestic policy through covert funding of demonstrations.
7. Transparency promotes accountability and public trust.

**SEC. 3. DEFINITIONS**
* Demonstration -- A public protest, rally, march, or organized gathering intended to influence public opinion or public policy.
* Compensated Participant -- An individual receiving financial or material compensation for participating in a demonstration, excluding reasonable expense reimbursement.
* Sponsoring Entity -- Any individual or organization that organizes, funds, or directs demonstration activity, including political parties, advocacy groups, and affiliated networks.
* Coordinated Demonstration Campaign -- Demonstrations organized across multiple jurisdictions by a common entity or affiliated network.
* Aggregated Funding -- Multiple contributions originating from the same individual, entity, or coordinated source that, when combined, exceed disclosure thresholds.

**SEC. 4. DISCLOSURE OF DEMONSTRATION FUNDING**
(a) Any Sponsoring Entity that expends more than $1,500 organizing demonstration activity shall file a disclosure report.
(b) The report shall include:
* identity of the sponsoring entity
* total funds expended
* funding sources above $1,000
* whether compensated participants were utilized and a separate requirement for their registration and compensation.

(c) Aggregation Rule
For purposes of this section, multiple contributions from the same source shall be aggregated.
If aggregated contributions exceed $1,500, disclosure is required.
(d) Reports shall be filed within 10 days of the demonstration.
**SEC. 5. EVASION AND PENALTIES**
(a) It shall be unlawful to knowingly structure, divide, or route contributions to evade disclosure requirements.
(b) Violations may result in:
* civil fines
* enhanced penalties for willful violations
* additional liability where evasion contributed to public harm

(c) Evidence of structured or aggregated funding designed to avoid disclosure may be considered prima facie evidence of intent to evade transparency requirements.
**SEC. 6. COORDINATED DEMONSTRATION CAMPAIGNS**
Entities organizing demonstrations across multiple jurisdictions shall disclose:
* participating affiliates
* jurisdictions involved
* total funding
* number of compensated participants.

**SEC. 7. FOREIGN-FUNDED DEMONSTRATION RESTRICTIONS**
(a) It shall be unlawful for any foreign government or foreign-controlled entity to fund or materially support demonstration activity where such activity is intended to:
1. support terrorism or hostage-taking;
2. incite or contribute to violence against civilians;
3. create a reasonable risk of threats to human life.

(b) Enforcement shall align with existing federal law, including the Foreign Agents Registration Act.
**SEC. 8. FOREIGN FUNDING DISCLOSURE**
Any domestic entity receiving foreign funds used for demonstration activity shall disclose:
* the foreign source
* the amount received
* the purpose of such funding.

**SEC. 9. LIABILITY FOR ORGANIZED UNLAWFUL ACTIVITY**
A Sponsoring Entity may be held civilly liable where it knowingly organizes or materially supports demonstration activity involving unlawful conduct resulting in:
* bodily injury
* death
* property destruction.

**SEC. 10. CIVIL CAUSE OF ACTION**
Any person or entity injured by unlawful conduct during a demonstration may bring a civil action against responsible parties, including Sponsoring Entities.
**SEC. 11. RULE OF CONSTRUCTION**
Nothing in this Act shall be construed to:
* prohibit peaceful protest
* regulate viewpoints
* require disclosure of personal beliefs.

**SEC. 12. SEVERABILITY**
If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall remain in effect.
* * *
**Final Message**
This weekend may be about "No Kings" for some, But it should also be about something equally important:
**No hidden sponsors. No fake movements. No hidden leaders pulling the strings. Just real protest and exercise of Constitutionally protected free speech that is "Free"!**

Friends,
We’re coming up on a critical end-of-month fundraising deadline, and I’ll be direct, we’re falling short of where we need to be. I’m working every day in Congress to deliver results for Wisconsin families, but I can’t keep fighting without your support.

And with potential redistricting battles looming, the stakes couldn’t be higher. Leaders We Deserve endorsed Randy because he represents exactly the kind of leadership our generation needs.
Randy grew up in California’s Central Valley in a working-class immigrant family. He helped his parents run a small auto shop, and like so many families, they relied on public schools and health care programs to get by.
From fixing cars to earning his PhD, Randy knows what it means to work hard and still face an uphill climb.
Now he’s running for Congress to fight for families like his own, and he’s doing it without taking a dime of corporate PAC money.

Five years ago, I gathered with patriots from all corners of America to protest the certification of the 2020 election results.

All we wanted was for President Trump to get a fair shake, for mail-in vote counts to be redone, and to ensure no fraud had taken place. However, President Trump's enemies saw us coming, and they were ready and waiting to pull off perhaps the biggest psy-op America has ever seen.

Capitol Police officers welcomed many J6ers into the building, with some even providing off-the-cuff tours as they ushered protestors through the halls of the Capitol.

Friend, Five years ago, I gathered with patriots from all corners of America to protest the certification of the 2020 election results. All we wanted was for President Trump to get a fair shake, for mail-in vote counts to be redone, and to ensure no fraud had taken place. However, President Trump's enemies saw us coming, and they were ready and waiting to pull off perhaps the biggest psy-op America has ever seen. Capitol Police officers welcomed many J6ers into the building, with some even providing off-the-cuff tours as they ushered protestors through the halls of the Capitol. All of a sudden, though, things took a very dark turn... A Capitol Police officer murdered Ashli Babbitt. Overzealous officers assaulted protestors. Rosann Boyland was trampled to death in the panic that ensued as the Capitol Police swiftly turned on peaceful protestors. For many, like myself, this day marked the beginning of a years-long political persecution that tore families apart, devastated finances, and even denied many of us our freedom and our fundamental human rights. It also motivated me to start Stand in the Gap -- a commitment to stand in solidarity with and fight for those who are being overlooked or mistreated. Our goal is to provide support and advocacy for those in need, ensuring they aren't left to face their challenges alone. Stand in the Gap originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping the recently released J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. Surprisingly, there are very few resources for people who are released from prison, particularly if they are conservative, America First activists, or who supported President Trump. These J6ers are our neighbors. They are sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, mothers and fathers. It is up to us to ensure that they have the resources needed to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. We were founded to "stand in the gap" for those in prison and those navigating life after incarceration. Our mission is to ensure that every J6er receives the help they need to heal - physically, mentally, emotionally, spiritually, and financially - to reintegrate into society. But they need your help to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. Sincerely, Shane Jenkins Founder and Executive Director of Stand in the Gap P.S. body:

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | A Su-57 downed... Trust in
the Supreme Court is collapsing because this majority has shown exactly
who it serves: ideology over the law, power over precedent, and partisan
outcomes over accountability.

They said they would respect precedent. Then they overturned it.
They said they would defend the Constitution. Then they twisted it.
They said no one is above the law. Then they carved out exceptions for a
wannabe authoritarian president.

It's a captured, corrupt Court, plain and simple. And Americans see it.

The legitimacy of the Court depends on public trust — on the belief that
decisions are grounded in law, not ideology. But that trust is being
dismantled as a small group of justices reshape our rights and our
democracy without accountability.

The result? A judiciary that operates like a partisan weapon.

Demand Justice PAC was built for this moment. We’re not here to accept a
captured Court. We’re here to build a judiciary that answers to the
Constitution — not political donors, not ideological agendas, and not
unchecked power.

We’re leading the fight to:

* Expand the bench to break the grip of a supermajority.
* Establish term limits so no justice can cling to power for decades.
* Enforce a binding code of ethics to root out corruption.
* End the stranglehold of partisan control over our judiciary.

This is how we restore trust. This is how we protect our democracy. But we
cannot do it without you.

I can feel it in my conversations with friends, at work, at home—there's a real sense that things aren't moving in the right direction, and people are tired of it.

name: Gretchen Whitmer
subject: We can’t keep going like this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC
body:
They promised lower prices, and they haven’t delivered |
#
---
Folks, The American people were promised lower prices. Instead, they’re footing the bill for reckless tariffs and another costly conflict overseas. Gas has jumped by more than 70 cents in just a few weeks. Groceries and housing are still too expensive. body:
Too many Democrats are still asleep at the wheel.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260328-1&t=1&akid=3302%2E587540%2EgA_rU8)
Peter, I’m not pulling any punches here:
**The end-of-quarter fundraising deadline is just a few days out — and this is a critical moment for Leaders We Deserve to prove the strength of our grassroots movement.**
**[If you’re with me in the fight to elect the next generation of progressive leaders, can you make a $5 contribution now toward our $100,000 goal before the deadline?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260328_1_eoq.GBjFZ4&refcode=em20260328-3302&amount=5&t=2&akid=3302%2E587540%2EgA_rU8)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260328_1_eoq.GBjFZ4&amount=5&refcode=em20260328-3302&t=21&akid=3302%2E587540%2EgA_rU8)**
Let’s not sugarcoat it, Peter: Too many Democrats are still asleep at the wheel while Trump and the GOP are charging full speed ahead with a radical, dangerous agenda.
And too often, we’re told to just “stay the course,” even when that course has failed millions of Americans. Well, I don’t think it’s controversial to say: _That’s not good enough._
Not when our party is losing ground with young voters, working families, and so many people who’ve stopped believing that the government can actually deliver for them.
We’re here to change that — but we have to do it together. The other side has right-wing billionaires, corporate PACs, and entrenched special interests. But we’ve got something even more powerful than all of that. **We’ve got the undeniable power of people like you.**
**Look at what happened in New York City last summer when we elected Zohran Mamdani. Look at what’s happening across the country as our young progressive candidates like Christian Menefee and Demi Palecek are upending the status quo.**
We can keep fueling victories like these all across the country, electing bold young leaders who will actually fight for us. We can elect a new generation of Democrats with the fire, urgency, and clarity to not only meet this moment, but also to provide a real vision for the future.
**[But we can only do it together. Can you pitch in $5 right now to join the fight?**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260328_1_eoq.GBjFZ4&amount=5&refcode=em20260328-3302&t=23&akid=3302%2E587540%2EgA_rU8)** ](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260328_1_eoq.GBjFZ4&refcode=em20260328-3302&amount=5&t=22&akid=3302%2E587540%2EgA_rU8)**
Thank you for your support ahead of this crucial deadline.
David

body:
